In-scope systems.value: SERFF Filing Rules + Filing Access; determinations logged in the filing tracker

Compliance procedure documented.value: Filing Determination Procedure (pre-use gate) — intake, classification, per-state review-method lookup, exemption basis, deemer math, log entry

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Chief Compliance Officer; reviewed annually and on any state filing-rule bulletin

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing — determination must close before the product build freeze; prior-approval states drive the latest-submission date backed off the target effective date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker milestone alerts at T-90/T-60/T-30 days to target effective date for every open determination

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Determination worksheet, dated state filing-rules captures and counsel sign-off retained 7 years from form/rate withdrawal

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any change implemented without a determination is logged as a compliance exception with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off every 'no filing required' call and every late/unfiled remediation

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All product/form/rate/rule changes implemented in the quarter per the policy admin change log, across all writing companies and states

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any implemented change with no determination on file before its effective date is a fail; ≥1 fail escalates to the CCO

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per-filing; test runs quarterly over that quarter's population plus 100% review of prior-approval states

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have authored any sampled determination

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Determination log export + SERFF tracking numbers + approval letters, presentable as a market conduct exam response within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct Compliance owns the exam/inquiry response; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of an unfiled change before it is sent

checklist.step: Take in the approved product change and open a determination worksheet
actions: Open the product change queue and filter Status = 'Approved for filing determination'.
Copy onto a new determination worksheet: product name, writing company and NAIC co-code, TOI/Sub-TOI, target effective date, affected states, new-business-only vs new + in-force.
Ask the Insurance Product Manager for the business driver and the hard date driver (competitor response, statutory mandate, release train) and record it.
Attach the signed change request to the determination folder named <company>-<TOI>-<effective date>.
checklist.done: the worksheet carries product, company, TOI/Sub-TOI, target date and state list, with the change request attached.

checklist.step: Break the change into filable elements and tag each one
actions: List every artifact the change touches on its own worksheet row.

Tag each row FORM (policy form, endorsement, application, rider, notice), RATE (base rates, factors, tiers, territory relativities), RULE (eligibility/underwriting rule, manual page) or NON-FILED (marketing collateral, internal procedure).
For FORM rows copy the form number and edition date exactly as printed in the form footer.
For RATE rows get the statewide rate level impact % per state from Pricing and paste it on the row.
Email the Pricing Actuary to confirm the rate level impact figures in writing; file the reply.
checklist.done: every touched artifact has a row, a tag, and (for rate rows) a written rate level impact % from Pricing.

checklist.step: Collect the filing-grade source artifacts from Product Development and Pricing
actions: Request from Product Development: print-ready form PDFs with form number and edition date on every page, plus a redline against the currently approved edition.
Request from Pricing: rate exhibits, rating manual pages and the draft actuarial memorandum with the certification page.
Open every PDF and check it is text-searchable, watermark-free, and under the SERFF attachment size cap (3 MB per attachment as a rule of thumb).
Reject and re-request anything marked DRAFT or missing an edition date rather than filing around it.
Save the accepted set into the determination folder.
checklist.done: the artifact set is complete, watermark-free, and the redline scope matches the change request scope.

checklist.step: Read each affected state's current SERFF filing rules for this TOI
actions: Log in to SERFF (login.serff.com) with the company instance and your industry user id.
From the Industry menu open 'Filing Rules', or open the state's entry in the NAIC Product Requirements Locator.
Select the state, then the Business Type and the TOI/Sub-TOI matching the change.
Read the state's General Instructions and open any attached filing-requirements checklist or state-specific transmittal.
Print the instructions page to PDF, name it <state>-filing-rules-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and file it — this is the evidence behind the review-method call.
Repeat for every affected state and note any bulletins the instructions reference.
checklist.done: a dated filing-rules capture exists in the folder for every affected state.

checklist.step: Record the review method per state per element
actions: On each worksheet row, set the review method: PRIOR APPROVAL, FILE-AND-USE, USE-AND-FILE, INFORMATIONAL/FILE-FOR-RECORD or EXEMPT.
Paste the exact sentence from the state instructions plus the statutory or bulletin cite you relied on into the row.
Where the instructions are silent or ambiguous, email the state's SERFF contact from the state's SERFF page and log the question, date and answer on the row.
Highlight every PRIOR APPROVAL state — those set the critical path.
checklist.done: every state/element row has a review method, a quoted source sentence and a citation.

checklist.step: Confirm the product coding and the submission channel each state accepts
actions: Open the NAIC Uniform Product Coding Matrix for the line and locate the TOI and Sub-TOI that match the product.
Check the state's SERFF Filing Rules page lists that TOI as accepted through SERFF.
Where the state takes the line outside SERFF, record the alternate channel (state portal URL or paper filing address) and its own instructions.
Write TOI, Sub-TOI and submission channel onto every state row.
checklist.done: TOI, Sub-TOI and submission channel are recorded and agree with the coding matrix for every state.

checklist.step: Support every 'no filing required' call with a named exemption
actions: For each EXEMPT/NON-FILED row, name the basis: commercial large-risk or exempt commercial purchaser exemption, surplus lines, non-filed inland marine class, informational-only material, or out-of-scope internal procedure.
Paste the statute, regulation or bulletin cite that grants the exemption, with its effective date.
Where the exemption depends on a threshold (premium size, insured net worth), record the tested value and where it came from.
Never leave a row reading only 'not required'.
checklist.done: every exempt row carries a named exemption, a citation and (where thresholds apply) the tested value.

checklist.step: Search SERFF Filing Access for an existing approval that already covers the change
actions: In SERFF open Filing Access and search by company (or NAIC co-code), state, TOI and form number.
Filter Disposition to Approved / Filed / Closed-Approved and sort by disposition date descending.
Open the closest match and compare the approved form edition and rate exhibit to the new edition.
Decide reuse vs new filing: reuse only where the approved text and rates are unchanged for that state.
Copy the SERFF Tracking Number and disposition date onto the worksheet row when reuse applies.
checklist.done: each row states reuse (with SERFF tracking number) or new filing, based on an inspected prior filing.

checklist.step: Compute the deemer clock and the latest submission date per state
actions: Read the review period / deemer days from the state instructions or statute (commonly 30, 45 or 60 days) and record it on the row.
Add the internal lead times: package preparation days, actuarial review days, and an objection-response buffer (10 business days is the working assumption).
Compute latest submission date = target effective date − (deemer days + objection buffer + implementation lead) and write it on the row.
Load each latest submission date into the filing calendar and set T-90/T-60/T-30 reminders against the target effective date.
checklist.done: every state row shows deemer days, the computed latest submission date, and a calendar entry with reminders.

checklist.step: Fix the package scope by listing what each state will demand with the filing
actions: From each state's filing-requirements checklist, list the companion items: actuarial memorandum and certification, rate/rule schedule, Statement of Variability, readability (Flesch) certification, side-by-side redline, cover letter, third-party filer authorization, filing fee amount and payment method (EFT vs check).
Name the owner and due date for each companion item and hand them to Pricing, Product Development or Legal as applicable.
Flag any item with a long lead time (Flesch scoring, translated forms, third-party authorization) so it starts now.
checklist.done: each state has a companion-item list with an owner and a due date ahead of the latest submission date.

checklist.step: Write the determination row into the Filing Determination Log
actions: For every state and element, add a log row: change id, state, element, filing required Y/N, review method, filing type, statutory cite, deemer days, latest submission date, reuse tracking number, decider and decision date.
Link the log row to the determination folder holding the dated filing-rules captures.
Set the log row status to 'Determined — pending counsel' where sign-off is required, otherwise 'Determined — closed'.
checklist.done: the log holds one complete, source-linked row per state per element with no blank fields.

checklist.step: Get Regulatory Counsel sign-off on the risky calls before closing the log rows
actions: Route to counsel every 'no filing required' determination and every prior-approval state row.
Counsel re-reads the cited statute/bulletin and either confirms or overturns the call in writing on the row.
Overturned rows go back to the Regulatory Filing Specialist for rework the same week.
Confirmed rows get counsel name and date stamped, then move to 'Determined — closed'.
checklist.done: no exempt or prior-approval row is closed without a dated counsel confirmation.

checklist.step: Publish the determination back to the product change record and arm the go-live gate
actions: Attach the determination summary to the product change record.
Set the release gate flag on every prior-approval state: no rate, form or rule may be used in that state until an approval or a satisfied deemer is recorded.
Give the implementation team the per-state earliest-use dates so the policy admin and rating configuration is dated accordingly.
Add the filing milestones to the product release plan.
checklist.done: the change record shows a per-state earliest-use date and prior-approval states are blocked in the release plan.

checklist.step: Escalate when the target effective date cannot survive the state's review timeline
actions: Compare the latest submission date to today plus the package-prep estimate for every state.
Where the date is already unreachable, raise an escalation to the Chief Compliance Officer and the product sponsor within one business day.
Present the options in writing: move the effective date, drop the state from the launch, or launch on the previously approved forms/rates.
Record the decision and its owner on the determination log row — skipping the filing is never one of the options.
checklist.done: every unreachable date has a written, owned decision that keeps the state either compliant or out of the launch.

checklist.step: Retain the determination evidence for the full retention period
actions: Move the determination folder (worksheet, dated filing-rules captures, counsel sign-offs, rate impact confirmations) into the compliance evidence repository under the product and effective date.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label so the record survives product sunset.
Confirm the repository index shows the record as searchable by state, form number and SERFF tracking number.
checklist.done: the determination record is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by state and form number.

testing.step: Build the population of changes that actually went live in the quarter
actions: Extract from the policy administration change log every form, rate, rule and manual change with an effective date inside the quarter, by writing company and state.
Add rating-engine configuration releases and manual-page publications so system-only changes cannot hide.
Reconcile the extract count to the release notes for the quarter and resolve any difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to release records and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every implemented change to a determination that pre-dates it
actions: Match each population row to a Filing Determination Log row on change id + state + element.
Check the determination decision date is earlier than the change's effective date.
List unmatched rows and late determinations as automatic exceptions — no judgement, no exceptions to the exception.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a pre-dated determination or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of rows in prior-approval states.
Take 25 rows selected at random (seeded, reproducible) from the remaining population, minimum 40 rows in total.
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every prior-approval state row.

testing.step: Re-perform the review-method call in SERFF for each sampled row
actions: Open SERFF Filing Rules (or the Product Requirements Locator) for the sampled state and TOI as of the determination date.
Read the General Instructions and reach your own review-method conclusion without looking at the worksheet first.
Compare to the recorded determination; any difference is an exception, including 'right answer, wrong citation'.
Screenshot the instructions page you relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled row has an independent re-performance note and a captured source page.

testing.step: Check the product coding and submission channel on the sample
actions: Look up the product in the NAIC Uniform Product Coding Matrix and compare the TOI/Sub-TOI to the determination row.
Confirm the recorded submission channel matches what the state's SERFF page accepts for that TOI.
Flag miscoded rows — a wrong TOI usually means the wrong instructions were read.
testing.done: TOI, Sub-TOI and channel agree with the coding matrix for every sampled row, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Test the support behind every 'no filing required' call in the sample
actions: Pull each exempt row and read the cited statute, regulation or bulletin as it read on the determination date.
Confirm the exemption actually covers the element filed under it, including any premium or net-worth threshold and the tested value.
Confirm a dated counsel sign-off exists and pre-dates the go-live date.
Treat a generic 'not required' with no cite as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every exempt row is supported by a verified citation, tested threshold and dated counsel sign-off.

testing.step: Trace every 'filing required' row to a SERFF submission that pre-dates go-live
actions: In SERFF Filing Access, search the recorded SERFF Tracking Number for the sampled row.
Confirm the filing exists for the right company, state, TOI and form number/edition.
Read the submission date and the disposition (Filed / Approved / Closed) and compare both to the change's effective date.
Where reuse of a prior approval was claimed, open that prior filing and confirm the approved edition is genuinely the one in use.
Capture the SERFF filing detail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every filing-required row traces to a real SERFF filing submitted before the change went live.

testing.step: Recompute the deemer maths and prove the release gate held
actions: For 10 sampled prior-approval rows, recompute latest submission date = effective date − (deemer days + objection buffer + implementation lead).
Compare the actual submission date to the recomputed date and note any filing submitted late.
Check the policy admin/rating effective date is on or after the approval date or the satisfied deemer date.
Any use before approval or before a satisfied deemer is a reportable compliance breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: no sampled state was used before approval or a satisfied deemer, and deemer maths reconciles.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the change id, state, what was missed and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause (intake missed the change, wrong TOI, stale instructions, timeline crushed) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for use-before-approval breaches, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare to the zero-unfiled-change threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the evidence references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer — who authored none of the sampled determinations — sign the workpaper.
Report results and open breaches to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns assembly and completeness of the SERFF submission package; actuarial content owned by the Product / Filing Actuary

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Hawaii Revised Statutes Chapter 431 Articles 10/10D plus the Hawaii Insurance Division SERFF General Instructions and its Life/Health and P&C filing checklists, re-read at package build (also Alaska Title 21, Alabama Title 27)

In-scope processes.value: Filing package assembly — SERFF Filing Description, form schedule, rate/rule schedule, actuarial memorandum and certification, Statement of Variability, readability certification, state transmittal and third-party filer authorization for every rate/rule/form filing

In-scope systems.value: SERFF Industry ▸ Create Filing (Form, Rate/Rule and Supporting Documentation schedules); source PDFs staged from the document management repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: SERFF Filing Package Preparation Procedure — per-state checklist harvest, attachment naming and PDF standards, Filing Description drafting, actuarial memo certification, fee and EFT setup, pre-submission QC

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with the Chief Actuary countersigning the actuarial memorandum standards; refreshed each time a state reissues its SERFF filing checklist

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing — the package must be QC-complete and signed at least 5 business days before the latest submission date computed in the determination, so Hawaii's review clock can start on time

Deadline reminders configured.value: Package-build tasks in the filing tracker carry due dates keyed off the latest submission date, with reminders at T-30 (checklist harvest), T-15 (actuarial memo due) and T-5 (QC gate)

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The exact PDF set transmitted, the completed state checklist, the signed actuarial certification and the QC sign-off sheet retained 7 years from form/rate withdrawal

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Packages rejected by a state for incompleteness, and any attachment filed in the wrong schedule, are logged with the missing item, cause and re-submission date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off any package rebuilt after a state rejection and any Statement of Variability language change

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All SERFF filing packages assembled in the quarter, listed from the filing tracker by state, TOI and SERFF tracking number, including packages rejected or withdrawn before disposition

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if any required checklist item is missing from the transmitted package, if the actuarial memorandum is uncertified, or if an attachment sits in the wrong SERFF schedule; ≥5% package rejection rate for the quarter escalates to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per filing; testing runs quarterly across that quarter's packages with 100% coverage of any package a state rejected for incompleteness

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have assembled or QC'd any sampled package

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly filing-package completeness workpaper (package inventory, sampled checklists, attachment-by-schedule comparison, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: For any state request, the transmitted package, the state's own filing checklist marked up, and the signed actuarial certification can be produced from the archive within 3 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Filing Specialist answers Hawaii Insurance Division completeness queries through the SERFF filing correspondence thread; Regulatory Counsel clears anything touching form wording or variability

checklist.step: Open the filing shell in SERFF and lock the filing identity fields
actions: In SERFF choose Industry ▸ Create Filing, select the state (Hawaii for the representative filing) and the Business Type from the determination row.
Set TOI and Sub-TOI exactly as recorded on the determination worksheet, then set Filing Type (Form, Rate, Rule, or Form/Rate combined) and the Filing Company from the company list by NAIC co-code.
Enter the Company Tracking Number using the internal convention <company>-<state>-<TOI>-<yyyymm> so the filing tracker and SERFF reconcile.
Enter the Effective Date Requested (New Business and Renewal) taken from the product change record, not from the release plan.
Take the state and TOI back to the Product Filing Specialist for confirmation before any attachment is loaded.
checklist.done: the SERFF filing shell shows the state, TOI/Sub-TOI, filing type, filing company and company tracking number matching the determination worksheet.

checklist.step: Harvest the Hawaii-specific filing checklist and turn it into a build list
actions: In SERFF open Industry ▸ Filing Rules, select Hawaii and the TOI, and download the General Instructions plus any attached Hawaii Insurance Division filing-requirements checklist.
Cross-check the same TOI in the NAIC Product Requirements Locator entry for Hawaii for items the instructions omit.
Transcribe each required item into a build list row: item name, required Y/N, SERFF schedule it belongs on (Form, Rate/Rule, Supporting Documentation), owner and due date.
Flag Hawaii-specific items — HRS Chapter 431 readability requirements, the rate filing exhibit set, and the third-party filer authorization if a consultant transmits.
Save the dated instructions PDF as HI-filing-checklist-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf into the filing folder.
checklist.done: a build list exists with one row per state-required item, each mapped to a SERFF schedule, owner and due date.

checklist.step: Assemble the form schedule attachments to SERFF PDF standards
actions: Pull the final, approved form PDFs from the document management repository and confirm the form number and edition date print on every page footer.
Produce a side-by-side redline against the currently approved Hawaii edition for each revised form and save it for the Supporting Documentation schedule.
Flatten each PDF, remove DRAFT watermarks and confirm each file is text-searchable and under the SERFF 3 MB per-attachment working limit.
Name each file <form number>_<edition date>.pdf so the state reviewer can match it to the form schedule row.
Hand the finished set to the Regulatory Filing Specialist with a one-line description per form for the Form Schedule 'Form Name' and 'Action' fields (New / Revised / Replaced).
checklist.done: every form is a flattened, searchable, watermark-free PDF named by form number and edition, with a redline for each revision.

checklist.step: Build the rate and rule schedule exhibits
actions: Export the Hawaii rate pages, factor tables, territory relativities and rating algorithm changes from the pricing model, clearly labelled current vs proposed.
Compute the Hawaii statewide overall rate level change % and the maximum and minimum policyholder impact, and state the number of affected policyholders.
Produce the rate/rule schedule exhibit set: rate manual pages, rule pages, an exhibit summarising the rate level change, and the supporting experience exhibit.
Send the exhibits to the Product / Filing Actuary for review and record the review date on the build list.
checklist.done: Hawaii rate/rule exhibits exist with a stated statewide rate level change %, impact range and affected policyholder count, reviewed by the filing actuary.

checklist.step: Write and certify the actuarial memorandum
actions: Draft the actuarial memorandum covering: scope of change, data and experience period, methodology and assumptions, trend and loss development selections, credibility, expense and profit provisions, and the resulting indicated vs selected rate level.
For life/annuity forms add the nonforfeiture and reserve basis demonstration required under HRS Chapter 431 Article 10D.
Attach the signed actuarial certification page naming the qualified actuary, the ASOPs relied upon and the certification date.
Have the Chief Actuary review and countersign before the memo goes onto the Supporting Documentation schedule.
Mark the memo confidential in SERFF only where Hawaii's instructions permit a confidentiality request, and attach the request form when they do.
checklist.done: a dated, signed and countersigned actuarial memorandum with certification page is attached and its confidentiality treatment is documented.

checklist.step: Produce the Statement of Variability and readability certification
actions: List every bracketed or variable item in each filed form and, for each, state the permitted range or the fixed set of alternatives and the conditions under which each applies.
Confirm no variable item can change the scope of coverage, an exclusion, or a benefit trigger — those must be filed, not bracketed.
Run the Flesch Reading Ease score on each consumer-facing form and record the score, the words counted and the method used.
Sign the readability certification stating each form meets the Hawaii minimum score and attach it plus the Statement of Variability to the build list.
checklist.done: a Statement of Variability covering every bracketed item and a signed Flesch readability certification with per-form scores are ready to attach.

checklist.step: Draft the Filing Description and cover letter that the reviewer reads first
actions: Write the SERFF Filing Description: what is being filed, whether it is new or a revision, the form numbers and editions, the rate level change %, the requested effective dates, and whether it applies to new business only or new and renewal.
Name any previously approved Hawaii filing being replaced and give its SERFF Tracking Number and approval date.
State plainly what changed from the approved version and why — reviewers open objections when the description forces them to guess.
Prepare the cover letter on company letterhead with the filer's name, phone, email and the company NAIC co-code, and route it to the Regulatory Filing Specialist.
checklist.done: a Filing Description and cover letter exist naming forms, editions, rate impact, effective dates and any superseded SERFF tracking number.

checklist.step: Attach the transmittal, authorization and fee documents Hawaii requires
actions: Complete the state-specific transmittal / Filing Fee section in SERFF and enter the fee amount from Hawaii's current fee schedule.
Set the payment method to EFT where Hawaii accepts it and confirm the funding account with Treasury before submission; otherwise record the check number and mailing date.
If an outside filing consultant transmits, attach the third-party filer authorization letter signed by an officer of the filing company.
Attach any required certificate of compliance or officer certification named on the build list.
checklist.done: the fee amount, payment method and any third-party filer authorization are recorded in the filing and agree with Hawaii's fee schedule.

checklist.step: Load every attachment onto its correct SERFF schedule
actions: On the Form Schedule tab add one row per form with form number, edition date, form name, form type and action (New / Revised / Replaced), and attach the matching PDF.
On the Rate/Rule Schedule tab add the rate and rule exhibit rows with document name, affected form numbers, rate action and previous state filing number.

On the Supporting Documentation tab satisfy every listed requirement — actuarial memorandum, Statement of Variability, readability certification, redlines, cover letter — and never dismiss a requirement with 'not applicable' without the reason typed into the comment box.
Complete the Rate Information tab where the filing carries rates: overall percentage rate impact, written premium change, number of policyholders affected and effective date of last rate revision.
checklist.done: every build-list item is attached on its correct schedule and no Supporting Documentation requirement is left unsatisfied or blank.

checklist.step: Run the pre-submission completeness QC against the build list
actions: Walk the build list line by line against the SERFF filing and tick each item off only after opening the attachment and confirming it is the right document.
Check form numbers and edition dates on the Form Schedule rows character-for-character against the PDF footers.
Check the rate level change % on the Rate Information tab equals the figure in the actuarial memorandum.
Confirm the requested effective dates match the product change record and that no attachment carries a competitor's or another state's name.
Return the package to the Regulatory Filing Specialist with a written defect list if anything fails; do not correct it silently.
checklist.done: the build list is fully ticked with a dated QC sign-off, or a written defect list has been returned for rework.

checklist.step: Check the package against the same state's most recent objection history
actions: In SERFF Filing Access search the company's last three Hawaii filings on the same TOI and open their Objection Letters.
List the recurring objection themes (missing variability detail, unsupported trend selection, readability score not shown, wrong form action code).
Pre-answer each recurring theme inside this package — add the exhibit or the paragraph now rather than after the objection.
Note in the filing folder which objections were pre-answered and where.
checklist.done: each recurring Hawaii objection theme from the last three filings is either pre-answered in the package or noted as inapplicable with a reason.

checklist.step: Take the package through the internal approval gate
actions: Circulate the assembled package to Product, Pricing, Legal and Compliance for a single joint review meeting rather than serial email.
Confirm the filed forms and rates are the exact versions the implementation team will configure — any late change restarts the package build.
Record each reviewer's approval with name and date on the package approval sheet.
Freeze the package: no attachment may be swapped after the approval sheet is signed without a new QC pass.
checklist.done: the package approval sheet carries dated approvals from Product, Pricing, Legal and Compliance and the package is frozen.

checklist.step: Get Regulatory Counsel to clear the form wording and variability positions
actions: Read each filed form against HRS Chapter 431 mandatory provisions for the line and confirm every required provision is present.
Review the Statement of Variability and reject any bracketed item that could alter coverage scope, exclusions or benefit triggers.
Confirm the Filing Description makes no representation the forms do not support.
Sign and date the counsel clearance on the package approval sheet.
checklist.done: counsel has signed the clearance confirming mandatory provisions are present and no variable item alters coverage scope.

checklist.step: Archive the exact transmitted package before submission
actions: Copy the frozen attachment set, the completed build list, the QC sign-off and the approval sheet into the compliance evidence repository under company / state / TOI / effective date.
Record a file-level hash or version stamp so the archived copy can later be proved identical to what SERFF received.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label.
Index the record by form number, SERFF company tracking number and state.
checklist.done: an immutable, version-stamped copy of the exact package is in the evidence repository and indexed by form number and tracking number.

checklist.step: Replicate the package for the remaining jurisdictions and record the deltas
actions: Clone the Hawaii package as the base for the other affected states from the determination worksheet's state list.

For each state, re-run the Filing Rules checklist harvest and record only the deltas: extra certifications, different fee, different readability minimum, state-specific transmittal, state-specific form variations.
Where a state requires a different form edition or rate exhibit, create a separate attachment set rather than filing the Hawaii version.
Log per-state package readiness on the filing tracker so submission can start as each state's package clears QC.
checklist.done: every affected state has a package with its own checklist deltas recorded and a readiness status on the filing tracker.

testing.step: Build the population of filing packages assembled in the quarter
actions: Export from the filing tracker every package with a build-complete or submitted date inside the quarter, with state, TOI, filing type, company tracking number and SERFF tracking number.
Add packages that were rejected, withdrawn or re-submitted so failed builds cannot drop out of the population.
Have the Product Filing Specialist confirm in writing that the export is complete for all writing companies.
testing.done: the package population is exported, includes rejected and withdrawn packages, and is confirmed complete in writing.

testing.step: Reconcile the tracker population to SERFF's own filing list
actions: In SERFF run Industry ▸ Filing Search by filing company and submission date range covering the quarter and export the result.
Match SERFF rows to tracker rows on SERFF Tracking Number and Company Tracking Number.
Investigate both directions: SERFF filings absent from the tracker, and tracker packages with no SERFF filing.
Record the reconciliation and its resolved differences in the workpaper before sampling.
testing.done: the tracker population reconciles to the SERFF filing search with every difference explained in writing.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample weighted to rate-bearing and rejected packages
actions: Take 100% of packages a state rejected or returned for incompleteness.
Take 100% of packages carrying a rate level change above 5%.
Take 20 further packages at random using a recorded seed from the remaining population.
Record the seed, population size, stratification rule and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from the recorded seed and covers every rejected and every high-rate-impact package.

testing.step: Re-perform the checklist harvest for each sampled state and TOI
actions: Open SERFF Industry ▸ Filing Rules for the sampled state and TOI and read the General Instructions and attached checklist as they stood on the package build date.
Write your own required-item list without first reading the team's build list.
Compare your list to the build list; any required item the build list omitted is an exception even if the state never objected.
Screenshot the instructions page relied upon into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled package has an independently derived required-item list compared line by line to the build list.

testing.step: Trace every required item to the attachment actually transmitted
actions: Open the sampled filing in SERFF and list what sits on the Form Schedule, Rate/Rule Schedule and Supporting Documentation tabs.
Open each attachment and confirm it is the document its schedule row claims, not a placeholder or a prior edition.
Confirm no Supporting Documentation requirement was bypassed and that every bypass comment states a reason.
Flag any attachment sitting on the wrong schedule as an exception — misfiled attachments are the most common cause of state rejection.
testing.done: every required item traces to an opened, correct attachment on the correct SERFF schedule, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify form numbers, edition dates and actions against the filed PDFs
actions: For each sampled package take the Form Schedule rows and open the attached PDFs.
Compare form number and edition date character-for-character between the schedule row and the PDF footer.
Confirm the action code (New / Revised / Replaced) matches reality by checking whether a prior Hawaii or other-state approval exists for that form number.
Confirm the archived repository copy is byte-identical to what SERFF holds using the stored version stamp.
testing.done: form numbers, edition dates and action codes agree across schedule row, PDF footer and archive copy for every sampled form.

testing.step: Re-perform the rate figures in the memorandum against the Rate Information tab
actions: Recompute the statewide overall rate level change % from the exhibits attached to the sampled filing.
Compare your figure to the number entered on the SERFF Rate Information tab and to the figure stated in the actuarial memorandum and Filing Description.
Recompute the maximum and minimum policyholder impact and the affected policyholder count from the same exhibits.
Any difference between the three stated figures is an exception regardless of size — states read this field first.
testing.done: the rate level %, impact range and policyholder count agree across exhibits, Rate Information tab, memorandum and Filing Description.

testing.step: Test the actuarial certification and the readability certification
actions: Confirm the sampled actuarial memorandum carries a signed certification page with the actuary's name, qualification statement and a date on or before the submission date.
Confirm the Chief Actuary countersignature exists where the internal procedure requires it.
Confirm the readability certification lists a Flesch score per consumer-facing form and that each score meets the sampled state's minimum.
Re-run the Flesch score on two forms per sampled package and compare to the certified score.
testing.done: certifications are signed, dated on or before submission, and the re-run Flesch scores agree with the certified scores.

testing.step: Log package-completeness exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the package, state, missing or misfiled item and the resulting state action if any.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: stale checklist, wrong schedule, uncertified actuarial content, form/edition mismatch, fee or authorization missing.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and where a state rejection occurred record the re-submission date and any lost review days.
Feed recurring root causes into the next revision of the SERFF Filing Package Preparation Procedure.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a remediation date and a procedure feedback note.

testing.step: Conclude the package-completeness test and obtain independent sign-off
actions: Compute the package rejection rate and the missing-required-item rate for the quarter and compare both to the 5% escalation threshold.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with references to the sampled packages behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who assembled and QC'd none of the sampled packages, sign the workpaper.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository and table the results at the next Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the rejection rate, missing-item rate, a conclusion and the committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Filing analyst who transmits and tracks to disposition; IIPRC-track submissions escalate to the Product Filing Specialist

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the IIPRC Uniform Standards and IIPRC Filing Information Notices for the product type, alongside Alabama Title 27 (an IIPRC member state), Georgia O.C.G.A. Title 33 and Kansas K.S.A. Chapter 40, re-read at submission

In-scope processes.value: Transmission and disposition tracking — choosing the IIPRC compact track versus state-by-state filing for life, annuity, LTC and disability products, submitting through SERFF, and driving every submission to a recorded disposition

In-scope systems.value: SERFF Industry ▸ Submit Filing with the Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Commission selected as the filing state; dispositions mirrored to the filing tracker

Compliance procedure documented.value: SERFF Submission and Disposition Tracking Procedure — compact-eligibility test, mix-and-match rules, submission, EFT fee payment, weekly status sweep, disposition capture and mandatory-state opt-out handling

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance; re-approved whenever the IIPRC amends a Uniform Standard applicable to the company's life and annuity portfolio

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing — IIPRC targets a 60-day review for standard product filings; the submission date, each objection response due date, and the disposition date are tracked against the product's target effective date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker sets a status-sweep reminder every 5 business days for open submissions, an alert at day 45 of an IIPRC review with no disposition, and a hard alert at day 30 before target effective date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: SERFF submission confirmation with tracking number and submission timestamp, all objection correspondence, the IIPRC or state disposition/approval letter and the final filed-form set, retained 7 years from withdrawal

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Submissions that stall past the review target, are disapproved, or are filed on the wrong track (compact vs state) are logged with cause, the states affected and the corrective submission

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off any re-filing after a disapproval and any decision to withdraw from the IIPRC track and file state-by-state

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All SERFF submissions transmitted in the quarter — IIPRC-track and state-track — plus all submissions open at quarter start, drawn from the SERFF filing search and the filing tracker

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if a submission has no captured disposition, no retained receipt id and submission date, or if a compact-eligible product was filed state-by-state without a documented reason; any product used before disposition is a reportable breach

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per filing; testing runs quarterly over transmitted and open submissions, with 100% coverage of IIPRC-track filings given the multi-state exposure

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have transmitted or tracked any sampled submission

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly submission and disposition workpaper (SERFF export, tracker reconciliation, disposition trace, aging analysis, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: For any IIPRC or member-state inquiry, the SERFF tracking number, submission timestamp, full correspondence thread and disposition letter can be produced within 3 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Filing Specialist answers through the SERFF filing correspondence thread; IIPRC Office inquiries and any member-state opt-out question route through Regulatory Counsel before reply

checklist.step: Test the product against IIPRC compact eligibility before choosing a track
actions: Confirm the product is one of the four compact-eligible lines — individual and group life, annuity, long-term care or disability income — and note the specific IIPRC Uniform Standard that governs it.
Read that Uniform Standard against the drafted forms and list every provision where the form departs from the standard.
Check the current IIPRC member-state list and identify which of the affected states are members and which (including any non-member) still need a direct state filing.
Check the IIPRC list of state opt-outs for the applicable Uniform Standard — an opt-out state must be filed directly even though it is a member.
Record the track decision (compact vs state-by-state vs hybrid) with its reason on the determination log row.
checklist.done: the track decision is recorded with the governing Uniform Standard, the member-state coverage list and every opt-out state carved out for direct filing.

checklist.step: Register the filing on the IIPRC track inside SERFF
actions: In SERFF create the filing and select 'Interstate Insurance Product Regulation Commission' as the filing state rather than an individual state such as Alabama.
Select the IIPRC Uniform Standard from the standards list so the filing routes to the correct reviewer queue.
On the States tab tick every member state the filing is to cover and confirm the company is licensed and in good standing in each.
Enter the IIPRC registration number for the filing company and confirm the company's IIPRC registration and annual fee are current.
Record the resulting SERFF Tracking Number on the filing tracker before proceeding.
checklist.done: the filing is registered on the IIPRC track with the correct Uniform Standard, the member-state list ticked and a SERFF tracking number recorded.

checklist.step: Complete the IIPRC-specific certifications and mix-and-match statement
actions: Complete the IIPRC Statement of Intent / filing certification confirming the forms comply with the named Uniform Standard in every respect.
Where any form is used with a state-approved form rather than a compact-approved one, complete the Mix and Match certification naming each state-approved form, its state and its approval date.
Attach the required IIPRC readability certification and Statement of Variability in the compact's own format — the state formats are not accepted.
Have an officer of the filing company sign the certifications and attach the signed PDFs to the Supporting Documentation schedule.
checklist.done: signed IIPRC certifications, the mix-and-match statement and compact-format variability and readability documents are attached.

checklist.step: Set up and confirm the filing fee payment before transmitting
actions: Compute the fee from the current IIPRC fee schedule: the per-filing compact fee plus each covered member state's own filing fee where the state charges one.
Enter the fee on the SERFF Filing Fees tab and select EFT, confirming the EFT account with Treasury the day before submission.
For any direct state filing running alongside (an opt-out state, or a non-member), enter that state's fee from its own fee schedule and its accepted payment method.
Screenshot the completed fee tab into the filing folder as proof of the amount tendered.
checklist.done: the compact and per-state fees are entered, funded and screenshotted, and the payment method matches what each recipient accepts.

checklist.step: Transmit the submission and capture the receipt evidence immediately
actions: Run the SERFF validation before submitting and clear every validation error — SERFF will not transmit an incomplete schedule set.
Press Submit Filing and wait for the status to move to Submitted to State / Submitted to IIPRC.
Capture straight away: the SERFF Tracking Number, the exact submission date and timestamp, the filing status and the list of states covered.
Export the SERFF filing summary to PDF and save it as the filing receipt in the filing folder.
Write the tracking number, submission timestamp and status onto the filing tracker row the same day — this is the receipt evidence the regulation demands.
checklist.done: the SERFF tracking number, submission timestamp, status and covered-state list are captured in the tracker and a receipt PDF is filed the same day.

checklist.step: Confirm the submission actually landed in every intended jurisdiction
actions: Open the filing's States tab the next business day and confirm each ticked member state shows a received status rather than an error.
Investigate any state showing 'not authorized' or a licensing block and resolve it with the Producer Compliance Manager or the state directly.
Confirm the parallel direct filings for opt-out and non-member states were transmitted and each has its own tracking number.
Update the tracker so every affected state from the determination worksheet has either a compact coverage flag or its own direct filing tracking number.
checklist.done: every state on the determination worksheet is covered either by the compact filing or by a direct filing with its own tracking number.

checklist.step: Open the disposition tracking record with computed target dates
actions: Create a tracking record holding: SERFF tracking number, track (IIPRC or state), submission date, review target date (submission + 60 days for a standard IIPRC review), target effective date and product release id.
Compute and store the slack days = target effective date − review target date, and flag negative slack immediately.
Set the 5-business-day status sweep reminder and the day-45 no-disposition alert.
Link the record to the archived package so anyone picking up the filing has the transmitted documents to hand.
checklist.done: a tracking record exists with submission date, review target, slack days, alerts armed and a link to the archived package.

checklist.step: Sweep filing status every five business days and record what changed
actions: In SERFF open Industry ▸ Filing Search filtered to Status = Submitted / Pending / Assigned for the filing company and export the open list.
For each open filing open the Correspondence tab and check for new Objection Letters, Notes to Filer or Amendment requests.
Update each tracker row with the current status, the reviewer name where shown and the date of the latest correspondence.
Escalate to the Product Filing Specialist any filing with no reviewer activity for 20 business days.
checklist.done: every open filing has a status update no older than five business days and stalled filings are escalated.

checklist.step: Chase a stalled review through the right channel rather than waiting
actions: Where an IIPRC filing passes day 45 with no disposition, post a polite status request on the SERFF Note to Reviewer thread quoting the tracking number and the target effective date.
Where there is still no movement by day 55, contact the IIPRC Office filing contact by email, attaching the SERFF tracking number and submission date.
For direct state filings, use the state's published SERFF contact rather than a general switchboard, and log the date, person and answer.
Never phone a reviewer without logging the call and its outcome on the tracker row.
checklist.done: each stalled filing has a dated, logged chase through the SERFF note thread or the published regulator contact.

checklist.step: Capture the disposition the day it lands
actions: Open the Disposition tab on the filing and read the disposition status (Approved / Filed / Closed-Approved / Disapproved / Withdrawn) and the disposition date.
Download the disposition report and, for compact filings, the IIPRC approval letter naming every state the approval covers.
Confirm the disposition lists the same form numbers and editions that were submitted — a partial approval that drops a form is not an approval of that form.
Write the disposition status, date and any per-state variation onto the tracker row and attach the letter.
checklist.done: the disposition status, date, covered states and covered form editions are recorded and the disposition letter is attached.

checklist.step: Handle disapprovals and partial approvals without letting the product slip through
actions: Read the disapproval or partial-approval reasoning against the governing IIPRC Uniform Standard or state statute.
Decide in writing between: amend and re-file on the compact track, withdraw and file state-by-state, or drop the affected state or form from the launch.
Where a form was dropped from an approval, instruct the Insurance Product Manager to remove it from the release scope the same day.
Sign and date the decision on the tracker row and set the re-filing owner and date.
checklist.done: every disapproval or partial approval has a dated, signed decision and any unapproved form is removed from the release scope.

checklist.step: Publish disposition outcomes to the product release plan
actions: Update the product change record with per-state approval dates and the earliest permitted use date for each state.
Mark states still pending disposition as blocked in the release plan so configuration cannot be switched on for them.
Tell the implementation team which form editions and rate versions the disposition actually approved.
Re-baseline the launch date where the approval timeline has moved it, and inform the product sponsor in writing.
checklist.done: the release plan shows per-state approval dates, blocked pending states and the approved form editions.

checklist.step: Reconcile the tracker to SERFF at month end
actions: Export all filings from SERFF Filing Search for the filing companies with any activity in the month.
Match to the filing tracker on SERFF tracking number and list both orphans: SERFF filings absent from the tracker and tracker rows with no SERFF filing.
Correct the tracker for genuine omissions and raise an issue where a filing was transmitted outside the tracked process.
Sign the reconciliation and file it with the month's compliance evidence.
checklist.done: a signed month-end reconciliation exists with no unexplained orphan on either side.

checklist.step: Archive the receipt, correspondence and disposition as one closed filing record
actions: Assemble the closed-filing record: submission receipt PDF, the transmitted package, every objection letter and response, the disposition report and the approval letter.
Store it under company / track / state / SERFF tracking number and apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label.
Confirm the record is retrievable by SERFF tracking number, form number and approval date.
Set the tracker row status to Closed only after the archive confirms the record is complete.
checklist.done: a complete closed-filing record is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by tracking number before the tracker row is closed.

checklist.step: Report submission and disposition status to the product governance forum
actions: Produce a monthly status view: filings submitted, open by age band, dispositions received, disapprovals and filings with negative slack to target effective date.
Name every filing whose review timeline now threatens a launch date and state the recommended action.
Table the view at the product governance forum and record the decisions taken against each threatened launch.
File the pack in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a monthly status pack has been tabled, with a named recommended action for every filing threatening a launch date.

testing.step: Build the population of submissions transmitted or open in the quarter
actions: Run SERFF Industry ▸ Filing Search for each filing company across the quarter with no status filter and export the result.
Add filings open at quarter start regardless of submission date so long-running reviews are captured.
Split the population into IIPRC-track and state-track submissions using the filing state field.
Have the Regulatory Filing Specialist confirm in writing that every filing company instance was searched.
testing.done: the submission population covers every filing company, both tracks, and all filings open at quarter start, confirmed in writing.

testing.step: Reconcile SERFF to the filing tracker in both directions
actions: Match SERFF rows to tracker rows on SERFF Tracking Number and Company Tracking Number.
List SERFF filings with no tracker row — these are submissions made outside the controlled process.
List tracker rows with no SERFF filing — these are either abandoned builds or filings sent through another channel.
Resolve every difference with the filing team and record the explanation before sampling.
testing.done: the two-way reconciliation is complete and every orphan on either side has a written explanation.

testing.step: Draw the sample with full coverage of compact-track filings
actions: Take 100% of IIPRC-track submissions given they bind multiple member states at once.
Take 100% of submissions with a disapproved, withdrawn or partially approved disposition.
Take 20 state-track submissions at random using a recorded seed from the remainder.
Record the seed, the stratification rule, the population size and the selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every compact-track and every adverse-disposition submission.

testing.step: Re-perform the compact-eligibility and track decision
actions: For each sampled product, read the IIPRC Uniform Standard for the product type and reach your own eligibility conclusion before reading the determination.
Check the IIPRC member-state list and opt-out list as they stood on the submission date against the states the filing claimed to cover.
Confirm every opt-out state and non-member state on the determination worksheet has its own direct filing with its own tracking number.
Treat a compact-eligible product filed state-by-state without a documented reason, and any opt-out state left uncovered, as exceptions.
testing.done: the track decision and state coverage are independently re-performed and every uncovered state is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify the receipt evidence trio for every sampled submission
actions: Open each sampled filing in SERFF and read the SERFF Tracking Number, submission date/timestamp and current status.
Compare all three to the values recorded on the filing tracker row and to the archived receipt PDF.
Confirm the archived receipt was created on or within one business day of the submission date, not retro-fitted later.
Any missing or mismatched element of receipt id, status or submission date is a fail against the regulation's pass condition.
testing.done: receipt id, status and submission date agree across SERFF, the tracker and the archived receipt for every sampled filing.

testing.step: Trace each sampled filing through to a recorded disposition
actions: Open the Disposition tab and read the disposition status, disposition date and the disposition report.
For compact filings, open the IIPRC approval letter and list the member states and form editions the approval actually covers.
Compare the covered form editions to those submitted and flag any form silently dropped from the approval.
Confirm the tracker row carries the same disposition status, date and covered-state list.
testing.done: every sampled filing traces to a disposition whose covered states and form editions match what the tracker records.

testing.step: Recompute review-clock ageing and slack against target effective dates
actions: For each sampled open filing recompute days in review = report date − submission date and compare to the 60-day IIPRC review target.
Recompute slack days = target effective date − (submission date + review target) and identify filings that were transmitted with negative slack from day one.
Check filings past day 45 with no disposition carry a logged chase on the SERFF note thread or with the IIPRC Office.
Check the 5-business-day status sweep was actually performed by comparing consecutive tracker update timestamps.
testing.done: ageing and slack are recomputed, and every filing past the alert threshold shows a logged chase and an unbroken sweep cadence.

testing.step: Prove no sampled product was used before its disposition
actions: For each sampled filing pull the first-issued policy date for the filed form and state from the policy administration platform.
Compare the first-issued date to the disposition date on the SERFF filing and to any state-specific approval date on the compact approval letter.
Where a state was covered by a compact approval, confirm that state appears on the approval letter and not merely on the submission's state list.
Any issuance before disposition is a reportable regulatory breach, escalated the same day, not a test exception.
testing.done: no sampled form was issued in any state before that state's disposition date, or the breach is escalated the same day.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, affected states and remediation
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the SERFF tracking number, the affected states and the failure — missing receipt evidence, uncaptured disposition, wrong track, uncovered opt-out state or use before disposition.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: eligibility misread, opt-out list stale, sweep skipped, disposition not mirrored, receipt not archived.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel for any use-before-disposition finding.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue naming affected states, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude the submission and disposition test with independent sign-off
actions: Compute the proportion of submissions with complete receipt evidence and the proportion with captured dispositions, and compare to the zero-tolerance threshold.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the sampled tracking numbers supporting it.
Have the independent reviewer, who transmitted or tracked none of the sampled filings, sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository and report breaches to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states receipt-evidence completeness, disposition-capture completeness, a conclusion and the committee reporting date.

Official Code Title 31 and Minnesota Statutes Chapters 59A–79A for the parallel states

In-scope systems.value: Per-state effective-dating and product activation switches in policy admin and the rating engine, gated by the filing tracker's approval evidence

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off every gate override, every deemer reliance decision and every self-report arising from a use-before-approval breach

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every state/product activation performed in the quarter in policy admin and the rating engine, joined to its filing tracker row, including activations later rolled back

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any activation without a recorded approval or satisfied deemer, or with an incomplete evidence trio, is a fail and a reportable breach; a single occurrence escalates to the Chief Compliance Officer

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per filing at go-live; testing runs quarterly over that quarter's activations with 100% coverage of prior-approval states and every deemer-reliance activation

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly release-gate workpaper (activation extract, evidence-trio checks, recomputed deemer dates, first-issued-policy trace, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: For any Alabama or other state inquiry, the gate record showing receipt id, status, submission date, approval/deemer date and the first policy issued in that state, producible within 3 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager owns any use-before-approval inquiry; Regulatory Counsel clears the response and any voluntary self-report before it is sent

checklist.step: Stand the gate up as a hard, per-state blocker in the release plan
actions: Create one gate record per state per filed element on the product release, seeded from the determination worksheet's state list.
Set each gate to BLOCKED by default and configure the product activation switch so it cannot be enabled for a state whose gate is blocked.
Name the single release authority permitted to move a gate to RELEASED and remove that permission from release managers and product sponsors.
Publish the gate board to the product release plan so the launch team sees blocked states in real time.
checklist.done: every state has a gate record defaulted to BLOCKED, wired to the activation switch, with a single named release authority.

checklist.step: Pull the evidence trio for each state from SERFF
actions: Open the state's filing in SERFF and read the SERFF Tracking Number, the current filing status and the submission date from the filing summary.
Screenshot the filing summary and the Disposition tab into the gate record — an entry typed from memory is not evidence.
Copy the three values onto the gate record fields receiptId, status and submissionDate exactly as SERFF shows them.
Where the filing ran on the IIPRC track, also record which member states the approval letter names.
checklist.done: each gate record holds receipt id, status and submission date copied from SERFF with a screenshot of the source screen.

checklist.step: Classify each state's gate condition against its review method
actions: Read the review method recorded on the determination row: PRIOR APPROVAL, FILE-AND-USE, USE-AND-FILE or INFORMATIONAL.
For PRIOR APPROVAL states set the gate condition to 'affirmative approval required' and record the required disposition values (Approved / Filed-Approved).
For deemer states set the condition to 'deemed approved after N days' and record N from the state statute or SERFF General Instructions, with the citation.
For FILE-AND-USE and INFORMATIONAL states set the condition to 'accepted submission on file' and record what acceptance looks like in that state.
Never carry a gate condition across from another state — Alabama's review period does not govern Minnesota.
checklist.done: each gate names its condition type, the required disposition or deemer day count, and the citation that sets it.

checklist.step: Compute the deemer date for every deemer-reliance state
actions: Compute deemer date = submission date + N statutory days, using calendar or business days exactly as the statute specifies.
Search the filing's Correspondence tab for any objection letter, extension request or disapproval — each of these stops or resets the clock.
Where the clock was stopped, restart it from the date the company's complete response was submitted and recompute.
Write the computed deemer date, the day-count basis and any clock-stop events onto the gate record.
checklist.done: each deemer state shows a computed deemer date with the day-count basis and every clock-stop event recorded.

checklist.step: Verify the approval covers the exact form editions and rate version being implemented
actions: List the form numbers and edition dates named on the state's disposition or approval letter.
Compare them line by line to the artifacts the implementation team is configuring, taken from the release build manifest.
Compare the approved rate version and effective date to the rating table version being deployed.
Any form, edition or rate version present in the build but absent from the approval keeps its state gate BLOCKED, regardless of launch pressure.
checklist.done: every artifact in the build manifest is named on the state's approval, or the state gate stays blocked.

checklist.step: Set the per-state earliest-use date and effective-date the configuration to it
actions: Set earliest-use date = the later of the approval or deemer date, the state-mandated effective date on the disposition, and the internal release date.
Enter that date as the product and rate effective date in the policy administration platform for that state, separately for new business and renewal where the filing distinguishes them.
Confirm the rating engine's rate table effective date matches, so a quote dated before the earliest-use date cannot pick up the new rates.
Screenshot the configured effective dates into the gate record.
checklist.done: policy admin and the rating engine both carry the state's earliest-use date as the effective date, evidenced by screenshot.

checklist.step: Prove the block actually holds before releasing anything
actions: In the pre-production environment attempt to quote and issue the new product in a state whose gate is BLOCKED and confirm the system refuses it.
Attempt to issue in a released state with an effective date one day before the earliest-use date and confirm the system refuses it.
Confirm the old approved form edition and rate version still issue correctly for that state, so blocking does not stop existing business.
Record the test case ids, screenshots and results in the release test evidence and hand them to the Policy Admin Ops Lead.
checklist.done: negative tests prove blocked states cannot issue and released states cannot back-date before the earliest-use date.

checklist.step: Release the gate state by state, never in bulk
actions: Open each gate record and confirm all four items: receipt id, status, submission date, and approval or satisfied deemer date.
Confirm the QA negative-test evidence is attached and the earliest-use date is configured.
Move only that state's gate to RELEASED, stamping releaser name, date and time.
Leave every unproven state BLOCKED — a partial launch is always preferable to an unapproved use.
Publish the released-state list back to the launch team and the contact centre.
checklist.done: each released state has a stamped release with the full evidence trio plus approval or deemer date, and unproven states remain blocked.

checklist.step: Refuse and document any request to override the gate
actions: Log any override request with requester, state, business reason and the launch date at risk.
State in writing the exposure: unapproved rate or form use, per-policy penalty exposure and market conduct exam consequence.
Route the request to Regulatory Counsel and the Chief Compliance Officer — no one below that level may approve an override.
Where an override is nonetheless granted, record it as a self-identified breach with a remediation and self-report plan from day one.
checklist.done: every override request is logged, priced for exposure, decided above CCO level and, if granted, opened as a breach.

checklist.step: Monitor for late regulator action after the gate is released
actions: Keep the filing on the status sweep for 30 days after a deemer-based release and check the Correspondence tab for a late objection or withdrawal-of-approval notice.
Where a state acts after go-live, notify the Policy Admin Ops Lead the same day and re-block the state.
Quantify the exposure: policies issued in that state between release and re-block, and the premium written.
Hand the exposure figures to Regulatory Counsel to decide on remediation or re-rating.
checklist.done: post-release regulator action is detected within one business day, the state is re-blocked and the issued-policy exposure is quantified.

checklist.step: Keep a rollback path ready for every released state
actions: Document, before release, the exact steps to revert the state to the previously approved form edition and rate version.
Confirm the prior version remains deployed and selectable rather than overwritten by the release.
Set the rollback owner and the maximum acceptable time to revert, and rehearse it once in pre-production.
Attach the rollback runbook to the gate record.
checklist.done: each released state has a rehearsed rollback runbook with a named owner and the prior approved version still deployable.

checklist.step: Reconcile released states to activated states weekly during the launch window
actions: Extract from policy admin the list of states where the new product, form edition or rate version is active.
Compare it to the gate board's RELEASED list and investigate any state active without a released gate the same day.
Check the rating engine's active rate versions against the same list so a rate can not be live where only forms were approved.
Record the reconciliation with the reviewer's name and the date.
checklist.done: the active-state list and the released-gate list agree every week of the launch window, with same-day investigation of differences.

checklist.step: Close the gate record with a complete pre-use evidence pack
actions: Assemble per state: SERFF receipt id, status and submission date screenshots, disposition or approval letter, deemer computation, configured effective-date screenshot, QA negative-test evidence and the release stamp.
File the pack in the compliance evidence repository under company / state / product / effective date with the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the pack is retrievable by state, form number and SERFF tracking number.
Set the gate record status to CLOSED only after the pack passes a completeness check.
checklist.done: each state's pre-use evidence pack is complete, retention-labelled and retrievable before its gate record is closed.

checklist.step: Report the launch's gate outcome to product governance
actions: Produce a launch close-out showing states released, states still blocked and why, any overrides, and any post-release regulator action.
State the number of policies issued per state and confirm the earliest issue date is on or after the state's earliest-use date.
Table the close-out at the product governance forum and record decisions on any state still blocked.
File the close-out with the launch evidence.
checklist.done: a tabled close-out shows per-state release status, first issue dates on or after earliest-use dates, and decisions on blocked states.

checklist.step: Feed gate failures back into the determination and package procedures
actions: Review every state that missed its planned launch date and attribute the cause: late determination, incomplete package, slow review or late implementation.
Where the cause was internal, direct the specific procedure change and set an owner and date.
Where the cause was regulator timing, adjust the standard lead-time assumptions used in the deemer and latest-submission maths.
Record the decisions in the compliance procedure change log.
checklist.done: every missed launch date has an attributed cause and either a procedure change or a revised lead-time assumption, with an owner.

testing.step: Build the population of state activations performed in the quarter
actions: Extract every product, form edition and rate version activation by state with an activation or effective date inside the quarter from the policy administration platform.
Add rating-engine rate table deployments so a rate activated without a form change cannot escape the population.
Include activations later rolled back, flagged as such.
Reconcile the extract to the release notes and have the Policy Admin Ops Lead confirm completeness in writing.
testing.done: the activation population reconciles to release records, includes rolled-back activations, and is confirmed complete in writing.

testing.step: Reconcile every activation to a gate record and a filing
actions: Match each activation to a gate record on product + state + element, and each gate record to a filing tracker row on SERFF tracking number.
List activations with no gate record — these are ungated go-lives and are automatic breaches.
List gate records showing RELEASED with no corresponding filing row.
Resolve every unmatched item with the filing team and record the explanation before sampling.
testing.done: every activation is matched to a gate record and a filing, or listed as an ungated go-live.

testing.step: Draw the sample covering all prior-approval and deemer-reliance activations
actions: Take 100% of activations in prior-approval states.
Take 100% of activations released on a satisfied deemer rather than an affirmative approval.
Take 20 further activations at random using a recorded seed from the remainder.
Record the seed, the stratification rule, the population size and the selection date.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every prior-approval and every deemer-reliance activation.

testing.step: Verify the evidence trio and approval date in SERFF for each sampled gate
actions: Open the sampled filing in SERFF and read the tracking number, status, submission date and disposition date directly from the filing.
Compare all four to the gate record's stored values and stored screenshots.
Confirm the screenshots were captured before the release stamp date rather than assembled afterwards.
Any missing or mismatched element of the trio is a fail against the regulation's pass condition.
testing.done: receipt id, status, submission date and approval date agree between SERFF and the gate record, with pre-release screenshots.

testing.step: Recompute every deemer date and re-test the clock-stop events
actions: Read the statutory review period for the sampled state from its statute or SERFF General Instructions as they stood on the submission date.
Recompute deemer date = submission date + N days on the correct calendar or business-day basis.
Open the filing's Correspondence tab and confirm no objection, extension or disapproval fell inside the window; where one did, recompute from the response date.
Compare your recomputed deemer date to the gate record's date and to the actual release date; a release before the recomputed date is a reportable breach.
testing.done: every deemer date is independently recomputed with clock-stops applied, and no release pre-dates the recomputed date.

testing.step: Trace the first policy issued in each sampled state
