actions: Query the policy administration platform for the earliest issue date of the filed form edition in the sampled state.
Compare it to the state's approval or recomputed deemer date and to the configured earliest-use date.
Do the same for the rating engine: the earliest quote or policy priced on the new rate version.
Any policy issued or priced before the approval or satisfied deemer is a reportable breach, escalated the same day.
testing.done: the earliest issued policy and earliest priced quote in each sampled state fall on or after the approval or satisfied deemer date.

testing.step: Confirm the approval actually covers the artifacts in production
actions: List the form numbers and editions and the rate version live in production for the sampled state.
Compare them to the form editions and rate version named on the state's disposition or IIPRC approval letter.
Flag any artifact live in production but absent from the approval, and any approved artifact never deployed.
For IIPRC-track approvals confirm the sampled state is named on the approval letter, not merely on the submission's state list.
testing.done: every production artifact in the sampled state is named on that state's approval, with differences logged.

testing.step: Test the gate control itself rather than only its output
actions: Confirm the activation switch is technically blocked for a BLOCKED gate by reviewing the QA negative-test evidence and re-running one case in pre-production.
Review the release-authority permission list and confirm no release manager or product sponsor can move a gate to RELEASED.
Pull the gate audit trail and check every RELEASED stamp carries a name, date and time.
Review every override in the quarter for CCO-level approval and counsel sign-off.
testing.done: the block is proven to hold in a re-run test, release authority is correctly restricted, and every override carries CCO and counsel sign-off.

testing.step: Log gate exceptions with exposure quantified
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the state, product, gate record and the failure — ungated activation, incomplete evidence trio, early release against the recomputed deemer, or unapproved artifact in production.
Quantify exposure for every use-before-approval finding: policies issued, premium written and the exposure window in days.
Assign a root cause and an owner, set a remediation date, and open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry each open exception into the next quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, quantified exposure in policies and premium, a root cause, an owner and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude the release-gate test with independent sign-off
actions: Compute the count of ungated activations and the count of releases pre-dating an approval or recomputed deemer against the zero-tolerance threshold.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the sampled states and tracking numbers behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who released no sampled gate and performed no sampled configuration, sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository and report every breach to the Compliance Committee and, where required, to the Audit Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states ungated-activation and early-release counts, a conclusion and the committee reporting dates.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns implementation of the approved forms and rates in policy admin and rating; configuration executed by the Configuration Engineer under change control

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Title 21 of the Alaska Statutes rate and form provisions with the Alaska Division of Insurance SERFF General Instructions requiring electronic submission and no paper pathway, plus Alabama Title 27 and the Arkansas Insurance Code for the companion states

In-scope processes.value: Implementation — configuring the approved Alaska form editions, rating tables, rules and manual pages into the policy administration and rating systems so what is issued matches what was filed and approved, with no unapproved variant deployed

In-scope systems.value: Policy admin product model, form library and effective dating plus the rating engine's rate tables and rule sets; change records raised in the ITSM platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Approved-Product Implementation Procedure — build from the approved artifact set only, per-state effective dating, form-library versioning, rating table load and reconciliation, output-document proofing, change record and post-deployment verification

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Information Officer and the Head of Compliance; re-approved when the policy admin or rating platform release model changes

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing — configuration must be complete and verified before the state's earliest-use date; Alaska's approved effective date, not the internal release train date, drives the configured effective date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Change records carry due dates keyed to each state's earliest-use date, with alerts at T-15 (build complete), T-5 (verification complete) and on the day approval lands for any state still unconfigured

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Change record, build manifest naming form numbers/editions and rate version, configuration screenshots, specimen issued documents and the post-deployment verification sign-off, retained 7 years from withdrawal

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any deployed form edition, rate value or rule not matching the approved filing is logged with the affected policies, the correction release and any customer remediation

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off any correction where policies were issued on an unapproved form edition or rate, including the re-issue or endorsement approach

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every policy admin and rating configuration release in the quarter carrying a filed form, rate, rule or manual page, joined to its approved SERFF filing and to the policies issued under it

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if any deployed form edition, rate factor or rule differs from the approved filing, or if a configured effective date pre-dates the state's earliest-use date; any policy issued on an unapproved variant is a reportable breach

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per filing at implementation; testing runs quarterly over that quarter's releases with 100% coverage of rate table deployments and new form editions

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built, tested or deployed any sampled configuration

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly implementation-fidelity workpaper (release extract, filed-vs-deployed comparisons, recalculated premium samples, specimen document trace, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: For an Alaska market conduct request, the approved filing, the build manifest, the deployed configuration extract and a specimen issued policy can be produced side by side within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager owns the exam response; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission that an unapproved form or rate was used before it is sent

checklist.step: Take delivery of the approved artifact set as the only build input
actions: Pull from the closed-filing record the Alaska approval letter, the approved form PDFs with their edition dates and the approved rate exhibits.

Produce a build manifest listing every artifact by form number and edition date, rate table name and version, rule id and manual page number, with the SERFF tracking number and approval date against each.
Mark the manifest as the sole permitted build input and state explicitly that drafts, working copies and pre-objection versions must not be used.
Hand the manifest and the approved artifacts to the Policy Admin Ops Lead and record the handover date.
checklist.done: a build manifest tied to the SERFF tracking number and approval date lists every approved artifact, handed over with a recorded date.

checklist.step: Raise the change record and bind it to the filing
actions: Raise a normal change record for the implementation, attaching the build manifest and the Alaska approval letter.
Enter the SERFF tracking number and the per-state earliest-use dates in the change record's regulatory fields so approvers can see the constraint.
Set the implementation window so deployment completes before the earliest earliest-use date across the affected states.
Route for CAB approval with Compliance named as a mandatory approver.
checklist.done: an approved change record exists carrying the SERFF tracking number, earliest-use dates and a Compliance approval.

checklist.step: Load the approved form editions into the policy admin form library
actions: In the policy admin form library create a new version for each form rather than overwriting the current edition, so the prior approved edition stays issuable.
Enter form number and edition date exactly as printed in the PDF footer and as named on the Alaska approval letter.
Attach the approved PDF or the templated version generated from it and record which it is.
Set the state applicability to Alaska only for Alaska-specific editions — never default a state-specific edition to all states.
Set the form's effective date to the state's earliest-use date for new business and renewal separately where the filing distinguishes them.
checklist.done: each approved form exists as a new, state-scoped library version with matching number, edition date and earliest-use effective date.

checklist.step: Configure the form trigger rules so the right edition prints for the right risk
actions: Translate each filed form's applicability — state, product, coverage, policy period, new business vs renewal — into the policy admin form-selection rules.
Configure the prior edition to continue attaching for policies effective before the earliest-use date, so back-dated and in-force transactions stay on their approved edition.
Where the filing replaced a form, configure the superseded form to stop attaching from the earliest-use date rather than deleting it.
Document each rule change against the manifest row it implements.
checklist.done: form-selection rules attach the approved edition from the earliest-use date and keep the prior edition for earlier effective dates.

checklist.step: Load the approved rate tables and rating algorithm changes
actions: Create a new rate version keyed to the Alaska approval and its effective date rather than editing the live version.
Load base rates, factor tables, territory relativities and any changed algorithm steps directly from the approved rate exhibits attached to the SERFF filing.
Enter the rate version effective date as the state's earliest-use date and confirm the prior version remains active for earlier effective dates.
Record the exhibit page number behind each loaded table on the change record so any value can be traced back to the filing.
checklist.done: a new Alaska rate version is loaded from the approved exhibits, effective-dated to the earliest-use date, with exhibit traceability per table.

checklist.step: Reconcile every loaded rate value back to the approved exhibit
actions: Export the loaded rate tables from the rating engine and place them beside the approved exhibits in a comparison workbook.
Run a cell-by-cell difference on base rates, every factor table and every territory relativity, and require a zero-difference result.
Investigate and resolve every non-zero cell before sign-off — a rounding difference is still an unapproved rate.
Sign the reconciliation with your name and date and attach it to the change record.
checklist.done: a signed cell-by-cell reconciliation shows zero differences between loaded rate tables and the approved exhibits.

checklist.step: Implement the filed rules and manual pages in the underwriting configuration
actions: Translate each filed eligibility, underwriting or rating rule into the underwriting workstation's rule configuration, quoting the manual page it comes from.
Confirm no rule is implemented more restrictively or more loosely than filed — both directions are deviations from the approved manual.
Publish the updated manual pages to the underwriting reference library with the same effective date as the forms and rates.
Have the Underwriting Director / Manager confirm the configured rules read the same as the filed manual pages.
checklist.done: filed rules are configured to match the approved manual pages exactly, with underwriting management confirmation and matching effective dates.

checklist.step: Test premium calculation against the actuary's independent recomputation
actions: Build a test-case set covering each Alaska rating dimension the filing changed: territory, coverage limit, deductible, class, tier and any new factor.
Quote each case in the pre-production environment on the new rate version and record the system premium.
Ask the Pricing Actuary to recompute the expected premium for each case straight from the approved exhibits, without sight of the system output.
Compare system to expected and require an exact match to the filed rounding rule; escalate any difference to the Configuration Engineer before deployment.
Attach the case set, both premium columns and the differences to the change record.
checklist.done: every rating test case matches the actuary's independent recomputation to the filed rounding rule, evidenced on the change record.

checklist.step: Proof the issued documents against the approved form PDFs
actions: Issue a specimen policy for Alaska in pre-production covering each new or revised form.

Compare the printed output page by page to the approved PDF: wording, form number, edition date, order of attachment and any bracketed variable resolved within the filed Statement of Variability range.
Confirm no internal watermark, draft marking or placeholder text reached the customer-facing output.
Sign the proofing sheet and attach the specimen documents to the change record.
checklist.done: specimen issued documents match the approved PDFs word for word, with a signed proofing sheet and specimens attached.

checklist.step: Verify effective dating cannot let an unapproved version issue early
actions: Quote an Alaska risk with an effective date one day before the earliest-use date and confirm the system selects the prior approved form edition and rate version.
Quote on the earliest-use date and confirm the new edition and version are selected.
Back-date a mid-term endorsement into the prior period and confirm it stays on the prior approved edition.
Record all three cases with screenshots in the release test evidence.
checklist.done: boundary tests show the new version selects only from the earliest-use date and back-dated transactions stay on the prior approved version.

checklist.step: Deploy to production inside the approved change window
actions: Confirm the change record holds the rate reconciliation, the QA premium comparison, the document proofing sheet and the boundary test evidence before starting deployment.
Deploy the form library versions, rate version and rule configuration together so no artifact goes live without its companions.
Record deployment start and finish times and the deployed version identifiers in the change record.
Do not deploy where any affected state's gate is still BLOCKED — deploy the configuration but leave the state inactive.
checklist.done: the deployment is executed inside the approved window with all verification evidence attached and version identifiers recorded.

checklist.step: Run the post-deployment verification in production before opening for business
actions: In production, quote and issue one controlled Alaska test policy on the new configuration and immediately void or cancel it flat.
Confirm the printed forms, form numbers, edition dates and calculated premium match the pre-production expected values.
Confirm the rate version and form versions shown on the policy record are the approved ones named in the build manifest.
Attach the production verification output to the change record and notify the Policy Admin Ops Lead.
checklist.done: a controlled production policy confirms approved form editions, rate version and premium, with the output attached to the change record.

checklist.step: Reconcile deployed configuration to the build manifest and the approval
actions: Extract the live form library versions, rate version and rule set for Alaska from production.
Compare line by line to the build manifest and to the artifacts named on the Alaska approval letter.
Flag any live artifact not on the approval, and any approved artifact never deployed, and route both to the Policy Admin Ops Lead the same day.
Sign the reconciliation and file it with the change record.
checklist.done: the production configuration reconciles item for item to the build manifest and the approval letter, signed and filed.

checklist.step: Watch the first weeks of issued business for configuration drift
actions: Build a daily report for the first 30 days of Alaska business showing form editions attached, rate version used and premium distribution against the pricing expectation.
Alert on any policy issued on a superseded or unapproved form edition, or on a rate version other than the approved one.
Compare actual average premium change to the filed statewide rate level change % and investigate a variance beyond 2 percentage points.
Report daily findings to the Policy Admin Ops Lead and weekly to Compliance.
checklist.done: a 30-day monitoring report runs daily, alerts on unapproved form or rate versions, and flags premium variance beyond 2 points against the filed rate level.

checklist.step: Close the implementation with a retained fidelity evidence pack
actions: Assemble the pack: build manifest, approval letter, change record, rate reconciliation, QA premium comparison, document proofing sheet, boundary tests, production verification and the configuration reconciliation.
File it in the compliance evidence repository under company / state / product / effective date with the 7-year retention label.
Confirm it is retrievable by form number, rate version and SERFF tracking number.
Close the change record only after the pack passes a completeness check.
checklist.done: a complete implementation-fidelity pack is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable before the change record is closed.

testing.step: Build the population of filed-artifact configuration releases in the quarter
actions: Export every change record deployed in the quarter that touched a form library version, rate table version, rating algorithm or filed rule, by state and product.
Add rate version deployments taken straight from the rating engine so releases outside the change process cannot hide.
Reconcile the two lists and treat any rating-engine deployment with no change record as an automatic exception.
Have the Policy Admin Ops Lead confirm the population is complete in writing.
testing.done: the release population reconciles the ITSM change list to the rating-engine deployment list, with unmatched deployments logged.

testing.step: Reconcile every release to an approved SERFF filing
actions: Match each release to a SERFF tracking number via the change record's regulatory fields.
Open the filing in SERFF and confirm the disposition is an approval covering the release's state and artifacts.
List releases with no SERFF tracking number or with a filing that is not yet disposed — these are automatic exceptions.
Record the reconciliation before sampling.
testing.done: every release is matched to a disposed, approving SERFF filing or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample covering all rate deployments and new form editions
actions: Take 100% of rate table and rating algorithm deployments.
Take 100% of releases introducing a new form edition in a prior-approval state.
Take 15 further releases at random using a recorded seed from the remainder.
Record the seed, stratification rule, population size and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every rate deployment and every new form edition in a prior-approval state.

testing.step: Compare deployed form editions to the approved filing artifact by artifact
actions: Extract the live form library entries for the sampled state and product, including form number, edition date, state applicability and effective date.
Open the SERFF filing's Form Schedule and the approval letter and list the approved form numbers and editions.
Compare both lists and flag any live form absent from the approval, any approved form missing from production, and any edition-date mismatch.
Confirm state applicability was not defaulted to all states for a state-specific edition.
testing.done: the live form library matches the approved Form Schedule on number, edition and state applicability, with differences logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the rate table comparison independently
actions: Export the live rate tables for the sampled state and version directly from the rating engine rather than reusing the team's reconciliation file.
Download the approved rate exhibits from the SERFF filing attachments.
Run your own cell-by-cell comparison across base rates, factors and territory relativities and record the count of differing cells.
Any differing cell is an exception, and any difference affecting issued policies is a reportable use of an unapproved rate.
testing.done: an independent cell-by-cell comparison of live rate tables to approved exhibits records zero differences, or logs each one.

testing.step: Recalculate premium on issued policies from the approved exhibits
actions: Select 25 policies issued in the sampled state under the new rate version, spread across territories, limits, deductibles and classes.
Pull each policy's rating inputs and the premium charged from the policy administration platform.
Recompute the premium from the approved SERFF rate exhibits and the filed rating algorithm, applying the filed rounding rule.
Compare to the premium charged; any difference outside the filed rounding tolerance is an overcharge or undercharge exception with a named policy number.
testing.done: all 25 recalculated premiums agree with the premium charged within the filed rounding rule, or each difference is logged by policy number.

testing.step: Trace issued policy documents back to the approved form PDFs
actions: Pull the issued document package for 10 sampled policies from the document repository.
Compare each attached form's number, edition date and wording to the approved PDF in the SERFF filing.
Confirm every bracketed variable resolved within the range stated in the filed Statement of Variability.
Flag any watermark, placeholder or superseded edition that reached a customer.
testing.done: issued documents for the sampled policies match the approved PDFs on number, edition, wording and variability range.

testing.step: Test effective dating on real transactions rather than test cases
actions: Query issued policies in the sampled state with effective dates spanning the earliest-use date, both sides.
Confirm policies effective before the earliest-use date carry the prior approved form edition and rate version.
Confirm policies effective on or after it carry the approved new edition and version.
Check back-dated endorsements written after go-live but effective earlier stayed on the prior approved version; any crossover is an exception.
testing.done: real issued transactions on both sides of the earliest-use date carry the correct approved versions, with crossovers logged.

testing.step: Log implementation-fidelity exceptions with policy-level impact
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the state, release, artifact and the failure — unapproved form edition live, rate cell mismatch, premium miscalculation, document variance or effective-date crossover.
Quantify the impact: policies issued on the unapproved artifact, premium over- or undercharged in total and per policy.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: built from a draft artifact, manual keying error, wrong effective date, rule mis-translation, deployment outside change control.
Assign an owner, a correction release date and, where customers were overcharged, a remediation approach cleared by Regulatory Counsel.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, quantified policy and premium impact, a fixed-list root cause, an owner and a cleared remediation approach.

testing.step: Conclude the implementation-fidelity test with independent sign-off
actions: Compute the artifact mismatch rate and the premium recalculation exception rate against the zero-difference threshold.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — citing the sampled releases and policy numbers.
Have the independent reviewer, who built, tested or deployed none of the sampled configuration, sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository and report unapproved-artifact findings to the Compliance Committee and the Chief Information Officer.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the artifact mismatch rate, premium exception rate, a conclusion and the reporting dates.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the objection response calendar and every reply posted to the state; substantive content owned by the Product / Filing Actuary or Policy Forms Specialist

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Title 21 of the Alaska Statutes and the Alaska Division of Insurance SERFF General Instructions setting the objection response period, re-read at each objection; Alabama Title 27 and the Arkansas Insurance Code for the parallel filings

In-scope processes.value: Objection handling — receipt of SERFF Objection Letters, Notes to Filer and interrogatories on open rate, rule and form filings, through drafting, internal clearance and posting the response inside the state's stated deadline

In-scope systems.value: SERFF Correspondence tab — Objection Letters, Response to Objection Letter and Note to Reviewer; response due dates mirrored to the filing tracker

Compliance procedure documented.value: Objection Response Procedure — daily correspondence sweep, due-date computation from the objection's own stated deadline, owner assignment by objection type, drafting and clearance, amendment handling, posting and closure

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance; reviewed annually and after any filing lost for failure to respond in time

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven — each objection carries its own response due date stated on the Objection Letter; where none is stated the internal standard is 10 business days, and any extension must be requested in writing before the original date

Deadline reminders configured.value: On logging an objection the tracker sets reminders at due date minus 5 business days, minus 2 business days and on the due date, escalating to the Product Filing Specialist at minus 2

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Objection letter, internal drafting thread, cleared response, any amended attachments and the SERFF posting confirmation with timestamp, retained 7 years from withdrawal

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Objections answered after the stated due date, closed without response, or answered without required clearance are logged with the days late, the state consequence and the root cause

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off every response that concedes a form or rate change, every extension request and every late response before it is posted

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every SERFF Objection Letter and interrogatory received in the quarter across all filing companies and both tracks, extracted from the SERFF correspondence records

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if any objection was answered after its stated due date without an approved written extension, or answered without the required actuarial or counsel clearance; a filing closed or disapproved for non-response is a reportable breach

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; testing runs quarterly over every objection received in the quarter — no sampling of the late population, which is tested 100%

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted or posted any sampled objection response

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly objection-handling workpaper (SERFF correspondence extract, due-date recomputation, timeliness analysis, clearance checks, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: For any state query, the objection letter, the posted response with its SERFF timestamp and the amended attachments are producible from the correspondence archive within 2 business days

Regulator response path.value: All substantive replies go through the SERFF Response to Objection Letter thread only; the Regulatory Filing Specialist is the single voice to the reviewer and Regulatory Counsel clears anything conceding a change

checklist.step: Sweep SERFF correspondence every business day for new objections
actions: Each morning open SERFF Industry ▸ Filing Search filtered to open filings for every filing company instance and review the Correspondence tab on each.
Confirm the SERFF email notification address is a monitored shared mailbox, not an individual's inbox, so a holiday cannot swallow an objection.
Open each new Objection Letter, Note to Filer or interrogatory and download it as PDF into the filing folder.
Log the objection on the filing tracker the same day with SERFF tracking number, state, receipt date and the reviewer's name.
checklist.done: every new objection is downloaded and logged on the day it appears, from a monitored shared mailbox and a daily portal sweep.

checklist.step: Read the objection and compute the response due date from its own terms
actions: Read the response deadline stated on the Alaska objection letter and record it verbatim, including whether it counts calendar or business days.
Where the letter states no deadline, check the state's SERFF General Instructions for a standard period and apply the internal 10-business-day standard only if the state is silent.
Record the due date, the basis for it and the source on the tracker row.
Set reminders at due date minus 5 and minus 2 business days and on the due date.
checklist.done: the response due date is recorded with its stated basis and source, and three reminders are armed against it.

checklist.step: Split the objection into discrete numbered questions and assign each an owner
actions: Number every distinct question or requirement in the objection letter, even where the state wrote them as prose.
Classify each: actuarial support, form wording, variability, rate level, compliance certification, or administrative (fee, signature, schedule placement).
Assign each to an owner — Product / Filing Actuary for actuarial, Policy Forms Specialist for wording and variability, Regulatory Filing Specialist for administrative.
Set each owner an internal draft-due date at least 3 business days before the state's due date.
checklist.done: every question is numbered, classified, assigned and given an internal draft-due date 3 business days ahead of the state's deadline.

checklist.step: Assess whether the objection asks for a change or only an explanation
actions: For each question decide: explanation only, amended attachment required, or substantive product change required.
Where a substantive change is required, tell the Insurance Product Manager the same day — the change may affect other states' filings and the implementation build.
Where the objection challenges an approach used in several states, list the other open filings that will likely attract the same objection.
Record the assessment on the tracker so the effort and the launch impact are visible immediately.
checklist.done: each question is classified as explanation, amendment or product change, with same-day notice to Product where a change is required.

checklist.step: Draft the actuarial answers with the exhibits the reviewer asked for
actions: Answer each actuarial question directly in the first sentence, then support it — reviewers reject responses that argue before answering.
Produce any requested exhibit: experience by year, loss development triangles, trend selections with the underlying data, expense support, or an alternative indication.
Where the state challenges a selection, state the data, the method and why the selection sits where it does, and give the indicated figure alongside the selected figure.
Where the state's point is right, say so and state the amended rate level rather than defending the original.
checklist.done: each actuarial question has a direct answer with the requested exhibit attached, and conceded points state the amended figure.

checklist.step: Draft the form wording and variability answers
actions: Quote the objected wording and the statutory or bulletin requirement the state cited side by side in the response.
Where a change is accepted, produce the amended form with a bumped edition date and a redline against the version originally filed.
Update the Statement of Variability wherever bracketed language changed and confirm no variable item now touches coverage scope, exclusions or benefit triggers.
Re-run the Flesch score on any form whose wording changed and update the readability certification.
checklist.done: wording answers quote requirement and text side by side, and every amended form has a new edition date, a redline and a refreshed readability score.

checklist.step: Clear the response internally before it goes anywhere near SERFF
actions: Read the assembled response against the objection letter question by question and confirm nothing is left unanswered.
Check no answer concedes a legal position, admits a past non-compliance, or promises something the company cannot operationally deliver.
Confirm the Chief Actuary has approved any amended rate level and the Insurance Product Manager any product change.
Sign and date the clearance on the tracker row before posting is permitted.
checklist.done: counsel clearance is signed and dated, every question is answered, and no answer concedes a legal position without approval.

checklist.step: Request an extension in writing before the deadline where the answer cannot be ready
actions: Where an owner will miss the internal draft date, post a Note to Reviewer in SERFF requesting an extension before the original due date, never after.
State the reason, the specific questions affected and the new date being requested.
Record the reviewer's reply and the granted date on the tracker and reset the reminders to the new date.
Where no extension is granted, post a partial response answering everything that is ready by the original due date and name the outstanding items with their dates.
checklist.done: any extension is requested in writing before the original due date and the granted or refused outcome is recorded with reset reminders.

checklist.step: Post the response through the SERFF objection thread
actions: Open the filing's Correspondence tab and use Response to Objection Letter — never email the reviewer separately, which leaves the filing record incomplete.
Answer each numbered objection item in the response body in the state's own numbering.
Attach amended forms, exhibits and certifications and, where a form or rate changed, also update the Form Schedule or Rate/Rule Schedule so the filing carries the current versions.
Submit, then capture the posting timestamp and the resulting filing status and write them to the tracker.
Export the posted response to PDF into the filing folder.
checklist.done: the response is posted in the SERFF objection thread with amended schedules updated, and the posting timestamp is recorded the same day.

checklist.step: Propagate an accepted change to every other open and future filing
actions: List every other open filing carrying the same form edition, rate approach or variability language that just changed.
Decide per filing whether to amend proactively or wait for that state's objection, and record the reason.
Where the change is proactive, instruct the Regulatory Filing Specialist to post an amendment on those filings citing the Alaska outcome.
Update the master form and rate library so future filings start from the amended version, not the superseded one.
checklist.done: every other affected open filing has a recorded amend-or-wait decision and the master library carries the amended version.

checklist.step: Track the objection through to closure or the next round
actions: Continue the daily correspondence sweep on the filing until the disposition lands — states frequently raise a second and third objection.
Log each further objection as a new tracker row with its own due date rather than appending to the first.
Where an objection round pushes the review past the target effective date, notify the Insurance Product Manager and the Policy Admin Ops Lead the same day.
Close the tracker row only when SERFF shows the objection resolved or the filing disposed.
checklist.done: each objection round is tracked as its own row with its own deadline, and launch impact is notified the day it becomes known.

checklist.step: Escalate a missed or at-risk deadline rather than quietly filing late
actions: At due date minus 2 business days, review every open objection with no cleared draft and escalate to the Product Filing Specialist and the owning function head.
Where a due date is already missed, log it as an exception the same day with days late and the reason.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the late response and decide whether to acknowledge the delay to the reviewer.
Where the state has closed or disapproved the filing for non-response, open a breach record and start the re-filing decision immediately.
checklist.done: at-risk objections are escalated 2 business days out and every missed deadline is logged the same day with counsel-cleared handling.

checklist.step: Archive the complete objection thread with the filing record
actions: File per objection round: the objection letter PDF, the internal draft and clearance record, the posted response PDF, the amended attachments and the SERFF posting timestamp.
Store under company / state / SERFF tracking number / objection round with the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label.
Confirm the thread is retrievable by SERFF tracking number and by objection receipt date.
Link the objection archive to the closed-filing record so the disposition and its correspondence stay together.
checklist.done: every objection round is archived with letter, clearance, posted response, amendments and timestamp, linked to the closed-filing record.

checklist.step: Analyse recurring objection themes and fix them upstream
actions: Each quarter tabulate objections by state, TOI and theme — actuarial support, wording, variability, readability, schedule placement, missing certification.
Identify the themes appearing in more than three filings and quantify the review days they cost.
Direct the specific package-preparation change that would pre-empt each recurring theme and set an owner and date.
Report the analysis and the resulting changes to the product governance forum.
checklist.done: a quarterly theme analysis names every theme appearing in more than three filings with a costed review-day impact and an owned package fix.

checklist.step: Keep the response calendar honest across holidays and absences
actions: Maintain a named backup for the correspondence sweep and confirm the backup has SERFF access before any planned absence.
Load state and federal holidays into the tracker's business-day calculation so business-day deadlines compute correctly.
Run a weekly check that every open filing has been swept in the last business day and that no objection sits unassigned.
Record the weekly check with the reviewer's name and date.
checklist.done: a named backup with portal access exists, holidays are loaded into the day-count calendar, and a weekly sweep-completeness check is recorded.

testing.step: Build the population of objections received in the quarter
actions: For each filing company instance, open every filing with activity in the quarter and export the Correspondence tab records.
Extract every Objection Letter, Note to Filer and interrogatory with its date, the filing's SERFF tracking number and the state.
Include objections on filings later withdrawn or disapproved so failed filings stay in the population.
Have the Regulatory Filing Specialist confirm in writing that every company instance was covered.
testing.done: the objection population is extracted from SERFF correspondence for every company instance and confirmed complete in writing.

testing.step: Reconcile SERFF objections to the filing tracker's objection log
actions: Match each SERFF objection to a tracker row on SERFF tracking number plus objection date.
List SERFF objections with no tracker row — an unlogged objection is a control failure whether or not it was answered.
List tracker rows with no SERFF objection.
Measure the logging lag = tracker creation date − SERFF objection date and flag anything beyond one business day.
testing.done: every SERFF objection reconciles to a tracker row and the logging lag is measured, with anything beyond one business day flagged.

testing.step: Test the whole late population and sample the rest
actions: Take 100% of objections whose response date exceeded the recorded due date, and 100% of objections on filings that were disapproved or closed.
Take 25 further objections at random using a recorded seed from the remaining population.
Record the seed, the stratification rule, the population size and the selection date.
State in the workpaper that late responses are tested exhaustively because the obligation is deadline-driven.
testing.done: every late and every adverse-outcome objection is in scope, plus a reproducible random sample of the remainder.

testing.step: Recompute each response due date from the objection letter itself
actions: Open each sampled Objection Letter and read the stated response deadline and its day-count basis.
Where the letter is silent, read the state's SERFF General Instructions as they stood on the objection date before falling back to the internal 10-business-day standard.
Recompute the due date applying the correct calendar or business-day basis and the state holiday calendar.
Compare your recomputed date to the date recorded on the tracker; a wrong due date is an exception even where the response happened to be timely.
testing.done: every sampled due date is independently recomputed from the letter and the state instructions, and differences are logged.

testing.step: Measure response timeliness against the recomputed due dates
actions: Read the posting timestamp of the Response to Objection Letter from the SERFF correspondence record — not the internal draft date.
Compute days late = posting date − recomputed due date for every sampled objection.
Where an extension is claimed, confirm the request was posted in SERFF before the original due date and that a granted date is recorded.
Confirm partial responses posted by the original date named the outstanding items and their dates.
testing.done: days-late is computed from the SERFF posting timestamp for every sampled objection, with extensions verified as pre-deadline and granted.

testing.step: Verify every objection question was actually answered
actions: Number the questions in the sampled objection letter independently of the team's numbering.
Map each to a paragraph in the posted response and to any attachment it references.
Flag unanswered questions, questions answered by cross-reference to a document that was not attached, and answers that restate the question without resolving it.
Confirm the response used the state's own numbering so the reviewer could follow it.
testing.done: every question in each sampled objection maps to a substantive answer and an attached supporting document, or is logged unanswered.

testing.step: Confirm required clearance preceded every posting
actions: For sampled responses containing actuarial content, confirm a dated Product / Filing Actuary or Chief Actuary approval pre-dates the posting timestamp.
For responses conceding a form or rate change, confirm a dated Regulatory Counsel clearance pre-dates the posting timestamp.
For responses following a missed deadline, confirm counsel cleared the late response.
A clearance dated after the posting is an exception even where the content was correct.
testing.done: every sampled response carries the required clearance dated before its SERFF posting timestamp.

testing.step: Trace amended forms and rates from the response into the filing and the build
actions: For sampled responses that amended a form or rate, confirm the SERFF Form Schedule or Rate/Rule Schedule was updated to the amended version rather than left on the original.
Confirm the amended form carries a new edition date and a redline against the originally filed version.
Trace the amended version into the build manifest and the deployed configuration for that state.
Any state issuing on the pre-amendment version after approval of the amended one is a reportable breach.
testing.done: every amendment is reflected on the SERFF schedules, carries a new edition date, and matches what was deployed for that state.

testing.step: Log objection-handling exceptions with the regulatory consequence
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the SERFF tracking number, state, objection date, days late and the consequence — review days lost, filing closed, disapproval, or launch date moved.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: sweep missed, due date miscomputed, owner unassigned, clearance bottleneck, extension requested late.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and open a breach record where a filing was closed or disapproved for non-response.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue naming days late and consequence, a fixed-list root cause, an owner and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude the objection-handling test with independent sign-off
actions: Compute the on-time response rate against the recomputed due dates and the count of filings adversely affected by non-response.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — citing the sampled tracking numbers and objection dates.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted or posted none of the sampled responses, sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository and report late-response trends and lost review days to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the on-time response rate, adverse-outcome count, a conclusion and the committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the filing archive and its retention schedule; content completeness certified by the Product Filing Specialist at filing closure

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — D.C. Official Code Title 31 rate and form filing and record-retention provisions together with the DISB SERFF General Instructions, re-read at each annual retention review

In-scope processes.value: Continuous archive maintenance — capturing for every District of Columbia and other-state SERFF filing the receipt id, current approval status and submission date, plus the approval correspondence and the exact filed form and rate versions, in a durable, retrievable repository

In-scope systems.value: The filing archive holding receipt/disposition evidence and filed artifact versions, indexed to the filing tracker and to the SERFF tracking number

Compliance procedure documented.value: Filing Records Retention Procedure — what constitutes a complete filing record, capture at submission and at disposition, indexing keys, retention clock from form/rate withdrawal, legal hold and disposal authorisation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the General Counsel as part of the enterprise records retention schedule; reviewed annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous — the receipt trio is captured within one business day of submission and the disposition within one business day of it landing; the retention clock runs 7 years from the date the form or rate is withdrawn from use, not from filing

Deadline reminders configured.value: Monthly completeness sweep on all filings closed in the month, an annual retention review each January, and a disposal-hold alert whenever a product is withdrawn so the retention clock starts on the right date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Per filing: SERFF receipt PDF with tracking number and submission timestamp, status history, objection correspondence, disposition report and approval letter, and the exact filed form editions and rate exhibits — 7 years from withdrawal, longer under legal hold

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missing receipt evidence, missing approval letters, unretrievable records and any premature disposal are logged with the affected filings, the reconstruction effort and the control fix

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel authorises every disposal batch and signs off any record reconstructed after a gap is found

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All filings with a disposition date in the trailing twelve months plus all archive records eligible for disposal in the period, listed from the filing tracker and the repository retention report

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Fail if any filing record lacks receipt id, status or submission date, lacks its approval letter or filed artifact versions, cannot be retrieved within the stated service level, or was disposed before its retention date; zero tolerance on premature disposal

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; a monthly completeness sweep runs on newly closed filings and a full retention and retrievability test runs annually over the trailing twelve months

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not maintain the archive nor have filed any sampled record

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual filing-archive workpaper (retention report, completeness matrix, retrieval timing tests, disposal authorisations, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: For a DISB or market conduct exam, any filing's receipt id, status, submission date, approval letter and the exact filed form and rate versions are producible within 3 business days of the request

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager assembles the exam production from the archive; General Counsel clears any statement that a record cannot be produced

checklist.step: Define what a complete filing record contains and publish it
actions: Write the record definition: SERFF receipt PDF with tracking number and submission timestamp, filing status history, the transmitted package, every objection letter and response, the disposition report, the approval letter and the exact filed form editions and rate exhibits.
State the three data points D.C. Official Code Title 31 compliance turns on — receipt id, current approval status and submission date — as mandatory fields, not attachments.
Publish the definition inside the Filing Records Retention Procedure and circulate it to the filing team and Document Management.
Have the Head of Compliance and General Counsel approve it as part of the enterprise retention schedule.
checklist.done: an approved, published record definition names every required component and flags receipt id, status and submission date as mandatory fields.

checklist.step: Capture the receipt trio into the archive at submission, not at closure
actions: Within one business day of transmitting a District of Columbia or other-state filing, create the archive record and populate receiptId, status and submissionDate from SERFF.
Attach the SERFF filing summary PDF captured at submission as the source evidence for those three fields.
Set the archive record state to OPEN and link it to the filing tracker row and the product change record.
Never leave the archive record to be created after disposition — the pre-implementation evidence must exist before the product goes live.
checklist.done: an archive record with receipt id, status, submission date and the source receipt PDF exists within one business day of every submission.

checklist.step: Refresh the stored status as the filing moves
actions: On each status sweep, compare the SERFF filing status to the status stored on the archive record.
Update the archive status field and append a dated status-history entry rather than overwriting — the history proves what was known before go-live.
Record each objection receipt and response posting as status-history entries with their SERFF timestamps.
Flag any filing whose stored status has not been refreshed in 30 days.
checklist.done: each archive record carries a dated status history refreshed on every sweep, with objections and responses timestamped.

checklist.step: Capture the disposition and approval correspondence the day it arrives
actions: Download the disposition report and the state or IIPRC approval letter from the SERFF Disposition tab within one business day of it appearing.
Attach both to the archive record and set the approvalDate, dispositionStatus and the list of form editions and rate versions the approval names.
Where the approval is partial, record explicitly which forms or rates were not approved.
Move the archive record state from OPEN to DISPOSED-CAPTURED.
checklist.done: the disposition report, approval letter, approval date and the approved artifact list are attached within one business day of disposition.

checklist.step: Freeze the exact filed and approved artifact versions in the archive
actions: Store an immutable copy of every form PDF and rate exhibit as filed, and where amended during objection handling, both the original and the amended version.
Apply a write-once or version-locked setting so an archived artifact cannot be replaced by a later edition.
Record a file hash or version stamp per artifact so the archived copy can be proved identical to what SERFF holds.
Confirm the archive holds the approved edition dates matching those named on the approval letter.
checklist.done: every filed and amended artifact is stored write-once with a hash, and edition dates match the approval letter.

checklist.step: Index every record so a regulator request can be answered by key, not by search
actions: Index each archive record by SERFF tracking number, company tracking number, NAIC co-code, state, TOI, form number, form edition date, rate version and approval date.
Confirm a lookup on any single one of those keys returns the whole record rather than a partial view.
Publish the index keys to Market Conduct Compliance so exam responses can be self-served.
Test one retrieval per key type each quarter and record the time taken.
checklist.done: every record is indexed on all named keys and a quarterly per-key retrieval test records the time taken.

checklist.step: Set the retention clock from withdrawal, not from filing
actions: Set each record's retention basis to 7 years from the date the form edition or rate version is withdrawn from use in that state.
Leave the retention date open while the artifact remains in use, so nothing becomes disposal-eligible while it is still issuing.
Take a monthly feed from the Policy Admin Ops Lead listing form editions and rate versions retired in the month, and stamp those withdrawal dates onto the matching records.
Confirm that in-force policies on a withdrawn form keep their record alive for the longer of the retention period and the policy's own run-off.
checklist.done: retention dates compute from a stamped withdrawal date fed monthly from policy admin, and remain open while an artifact is in use.

checklist.step: Run the monthly completeness sweep on newly closed filings
actions: List every filing whose disposition landed in the month from the filing tracker.

For each, check the archive record against the published record definition item by item — receipt id, status, submission date, package, correspondence, disposition, approval letter, artifact versions.
Chase the missing item from the Regulatory Filing Specialist with a 5-business-day deadline.
Sign the sweep with the count checked, the count complete and the open gaps.
checklist.done: a signed monthly sweep shows every filing closed in the month checked against the record definition with gaps chased to a deadline.

checklist.step: Reconcile the archive to SERFF so no filing is missing entirely
actions: Quarterly, export all filings from SERFF Filing Search for each filing company for the period and match to archive records on SERFF tracking number.
Investigate every SERFF filing with no archive record — this is the failure mode that leaves no pre-implementation evidence at all.
Investigate archive records with no SERFF filing, which usually indicates a keying error in the tracking number.
Record the reconciliation, its differences and their resolution.
checklist.done: a quarterly two-way reconciliation between SERFF and the archive is recorded with every difference resolved.

checklist.step: Protect records under legal hold from any retention action
actions: Maintain the list of matters — litigation, market conduct exam, regulatory inquiry — that place filings under hold, by state, product and form number.
Apply a hold flag to every matching archive record so disposal cannot run against it regardless of retention date.
Review holds quarterly and release only on written confirmation the matter has closed.
Record who applied and who released each hold, and when.
checklist.done: every record touched by an open matter carries a hold flag that blocks disposal, with applied and released events recorded by name and date.

checklist.step: Authorise disposal only through a reviewed, signed batch
actions: Produce a disposal-eligible list of records whose retention date has passed and which carry no hold flag.
Have the Product Filing Specialist confirm no listed form edition or rate version is still in use anywhere, including in-force run-off.
Route the batch to the General Counsel for written authorisation before anything is deleted.
Execute the disposal and keep a permanent disposal certificate listing what was destroyed, when, on whose authority and under which retention rule.
checklist.done: no record is disposed without a use check, written General Counsel authorisation and a permanent disposal certificate.

checklist.step: Prove the archive can actually produce an exam response
actions: Twice a year run a mock exam request: pick 10 District of Columbia and other-state filings at random and demand the full record.
Time the retrieval and check the pack contains receipt id, status, submission date, approval letter and the filed artifact versions.
Confirm the pack can be handed to a regulator without redaction problems or missing pages.
Log the elapsed time against the 3-business-day service level and raise an issue for any miss.
checklist.done: a twice-yearly mock exam produces complete packs for 10 filings inside the 3-business-day service level, with misses raised as issues.

checklist.step: Guard against silent loss when systems change
actions: Before any repository migration, upgrade or vendor change, take a full inventory count by record type and a hash sample.
After the change, re-count and re-hash the sample and require an exact match before decommissioning the source.
Confirm retention dates, hold flags and index keys survived the move.
Sign a migration assurance note and file it with the archive documentation.
checklist.done: every repository change carries a before-and-after count, hash sample match and confirmation that retention, holds and indexes survived.

checklist.step: Review the retention schedule against current state requirements annually
actions: Each January re-read the record-retention provisions of D.C. Official Code Title 31 and the equivalent provisions in the other filing states.
Compare the longest applicable period to the 7-year-from-withdrawal standard and raise the standard where any state demands more.
Record the states checked, the periods found and the resulting standard in the retention schedule.
Notify the Records Manager of any change so retention dates are recomputed across the archive.
checklist.done: an annual January review records the retention period found per state and any resulting change to the standard is applied across the archive.

checklist.step: Report archive health to the compliance governance forum
actions: Report quarterly: filings closed, records complete against the definition, open gaps by age, reconciliation differences, mock exam retrieval times and disposal batches authorised.
Name every filing still missing receipt id, status, submission date or approval letter and its remediation date.
Escalate any premature disposal or unretrievable record to the Audit Committee.
File the report in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a quarterly archive-health report names every incomplete record with a remediation date and escalates any premature disposal.

testing.step: Build the population of filings and disposal-eligible records for the period
actions: Export every filing with a disposition date in the trailing twelve months from the filing tracker, by company, state and SERFF tracking number.
Export the archive retention report listing records that became disposal-eligible in the period and records disposed.
Include withdrawn and disapproved filings, whose records must be retained as fully as approved ones.
Have the Records Manager confirm in writing that both exports are complete.
testing.done: the population covers all dispositions in the trailing twelve months and all disposal-eligible and disposed records, confirmed complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the archive to SERFF independently of the team's own reconciliation
actions: Run your own SERFF Filing Search per filing company across the twelve months and export the result.
Match to archive records on SERFF tracking number and list filings with no archive record at all.
For each missing record, determine whether the product was implemented — a filing with no record and a live product is a direct failure of the regulation's pass condition.
Record the reconciliation and its resolution before sampling.
testing.done: an independent SERFF-to-archive reconciliation lists every filing with no archive record and flags those whose product is live.

testing.step: Draw the sample across states, outcomes and disposal actions
actions: Take 100% of records disposed in the period and 100% of records under legal hold.
Take 100% of District of Columbia filings given the representative jurisdiction, and all disapproved or withdrawn filings.
Take 30 further records at random using a recorded seed, spread across states and TOIs.
Record the seed, the stratification rule, the population size and the selection date.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every disposed record, every held record and all District of Columbia and adverse-outcome filings.

testing.step: Test each sampled record against the published record definition
actions: Open each sampled archive record and tick the definition item by item: receipt id, status, submission date, transmitted package, correspondence, disposition report, approval letter, filed artifact versions.
Open every attachment rather than accepting a filename — a placeholder or an empty PDF is a missing item.
Record a completeness matrix with one row per record and one column per required item.
Any record missing receipt id, status or submission date is a fail against the regulation's pass condition regardless of what else is present.
testing.done: a completeness matrix covers every sampled record item by item, based on opened attachments rather than filenames.

testing.step: Verify the archived receipt data against SERFF itself
actions: For each sampled record, open the filing in SERFF and read the tracking number, submission date, current status and disposition date.
Compare each to the stored archive field values and to the archived receipt PDF.
Check the archived receipt PDF's creation date sits within one business day of the submission date, proving capture at submission rather than reconstruction later.
Flag any record where the stored status has not been refreshed since a later SERFF status change.
testing.done: archived receipt id, submission date, status and disposition agree with SERFF, and receipt PDFs were created within one business day of submission.

testing.step: Prove the archived artifact versions are the approved ones
actions: For each sampled record, list the form numbers, edition dates and rate versions held in the archive.
Compare them to the artifacts named on the approval letter and to the SERFF Form Schedule and Rate/Rule Schedule.
Recompute the stored file hash for three artifacts per record and confirm it matches the recorded value, proving the copy has not been replaced.
Where a form was amended during objection handling, confirm both the original and the amended version are retained.
testing.done: archived artifact versions match the approval letter and SERFF schedules, hashes re-verify, and amended forms retain both versions.

testing.step: Test retrieval by every published index key against the service level
actions: For 10 sampled records, retrieve each by SERFF tracking number, by form number, by state and by approval date in turn.
Time each retrieval from request to a complete pack in hand and compare to the 3-business-day service level.
Confirm each retrieval returns the whole record, not a partial view missing correspondence or artifacts.
Test one retrieval performed by a Market Conduct user rather than a Records Manager, to prove the archive is self-servable.
testing.done: retrieval by every index key returns a complete pack inside the service level, including one retrieval by a Market Conduct user.

testing.step: Recompute retention dates and test every disposal for authority
actions: For each sampled record recompute the retention date as withdrawal date + 7 years and compare to the stored retention date, checking the withdrawal date against the policy admin retirement feed.
Confirm no record whose form edition or rate version is still in use, or which supports in-force policies, carries a computed retention date at all.
For every disposed record, confirm the retention date had passed, no hold flag applied, the use check was performed and a written General Counsel authorisation exists.
Any disposal without all four is a zero-tolerance failure to be reported the same day.
testing.done: retention dates recompute correctly from stamped withdrawal dates and every disposal shows an expired retention date, no hold, a use check and written authorisation.

testing.step: Log archive exceptions with reconstruction effort and control fix
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the SERFF tracking number, state, the missing element and whether the underlying product is live.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: record created after disposition, status never refreshed, artifact not frozen, index key missing, hold not applied, withdrawal date never stamped.
Set the reconstruction plan — re-download from SERFF where still available — and name the owner and date; note where SERFF no longer holds the record and it is unrecoverable.
Escalate any unrecoverable gap on a live product and any premature disposal to the General Counsel the same day.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, a reconstruction plan with owner, and same-day escalation of unrecoverable gaps and premature disposals.

testing.step: Conclude the archive test with independent sign-off
actions: Compute the record completeness rate, the retrieval service-level attainment and the count of unauthorised or premature disposals.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — citing the sampled tracking numbers and the completeness matrix.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither maintains the archive nor filed any sampled record, sign the workpaper.
File the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository and report completeness, retrievability and any premature disposal to the Compliance Committee and the Audit Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the completeness rate, retrieval attainment, disposal exceptions, a conclusion and the committee reporting dates.
